# Ensure every Main Street card has dedicated card art (1024×1024 source)

## Problem statement

Every Main Street card renders a square art zone in its top-left corner, but
**108 of the 171 unique cards in `card-data.csv` currently render the same
generic `Fallback` sprite**, so the bulk of the deck is visually
indistinguishable. A player cannot tell an `Upgrade to Patisserie` from a
`Chef` from a `Rainy Day` at a glance, which undermines the 64×64 left-art
redesign's whole purpose.

## Users

- **Player (market / hand / street):** needs to recognise a card by its art
  without reading the title — especially when cards overlap in hand or stack
  on the street.
- **Content author:** needs a documented, testable rule for what art a card
  resolves to, so new cards cannot silently reintroduce `Fallback` art.
- **Engine maintainer:** needs one art-resolution path shared by the runtime
  generator and the static SVG exporter, guarded by a regression test.

User stories:

- As a player, when I look at the market, I can tell any two cards apart by
  their art alone.
- As an upgrade card, I show the art of the business I enhance under my new
  display name, so my purpose is obvious.
- As a content author, when I add a card to `card-data.csv`, the test suite
  tells me if I forgot to give it art.

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-26)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q1 | Art scope / strategy | **Option A — reuse-first.** Actively **duplicate the existing art under the new (card/display) name**, and produce **new art only where necessary** (no suitable existing art). |
| Q2 | Art production ownership | **The producer will produce the new sprites.** This item still owns the mapping, resolver, regeneration tooling and the drift guard. |
| Q3 | Event mapping granularity | **Map events by `trigger` × `targetSynergy` category** (a documented, generated mapping). |

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-29)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q4 | Source-art size | The producer provides **1024×1024** source art (`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`). The “64×64” is the on-card display zone, not the production size. |
| Q5 | Staff art granularity | **One sprite per staff role** (24 sprites). |
| Q6 | Event-category art | **Unique (bespoke) sprite per `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category** — representatives are not reused. |
| Q7 | Drift-guard tightening | **Yes** — tighten the guard to a strict “zero `Fallback` for every card in `card-data.csv`” assertion once the sprites land, in the same change. |
| Q8 | Duplicate-name clash | **Rename to remove the clashes**: business `Florist` → `Flower Shop`; event `Community Garden` → `Garden Party`. |

Art-production ownership (Q2, 2026-09-26) is unchanged: the producer supplies
all new source sprites.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-26, `dev` @ 933644bc)

Resolution path (all four card families call it with the card's `name`):

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` → `resolveCardArtName()` /
  `hasDedicatedCardArt()`: (1) spelling alias → (2) exact name → (3)
  `Fallback`.
- Map built by `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs`
  from committed `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` files into
  `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json`.
- A second consumer, `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`,
  duplicates the alias/lookup logic and must be kept in step.

Verified counts:

- `card-data.csv`: **173 rows / 171 unique names** (duplicate names across
  families: `Florist` = business + staff, `Community Garden` = community-space
  + event → name-keyed resolution shares one sprite).
- Committed sprites: **62 dedicated + `Fallback`** (63 map entries).
- Cards resolving today: **65** (63 exact + 2 via aliases).
- **Cards rendering `Fallback`: 108**:

| Family              | Cards | Resolving | Missing |
|---------------------|------:|----------:|--------:|
| business            |    30 |        28 |       2 |
| community-space     |     8 |         1 |       7 |
| upgrade             |    39 |         0 |      39 |
| staff               |    25 |         1 |      24 |
| event               |    71 |        35 |      36 |
| **Total**           |  **173** | **65** | **108** |

Every missing card already has an `art_notes` description in `card-data.csv`
(the source the existing 1024×1024 sprites were built from). There is **no
in-repo image generator** — the existing sprites were committed out-of-band
(commit `05026750`), and the producer will continue producing new art the same
way.

## Size clarification (reviewed 2026-09-29)

The “64×64” in the original title is the **on-card display zone** — a layout
dimension in SVG user units — **not** the size of the source art to produce.
Code review of the generator and renderer confirms three distinct layers:

| Layer | Size | Where | Role |
|-------|-----:|-------|------|
| On-card art zone | 64×64 | `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`GRAPHIC_*`) | SVG layout box only |
| Embedded bitmap | 256×256 | `src/card-art-map.json` (`artResolution`) | WebP `data:` URI in the SVG |
| **Source art** | **1024×1024** | `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` | Generator input |

`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` only loads files named
`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` (`SOURCE_SUFFIX = '_1024_x_1024.png'`) and downscales
each to 256×256 WebP (`ART_RESOLUTION = 256`). Phaser rasterises the card SVG
at `qualityScale = max(4, dpr)`, so the 64×64 zone needs a ≥256×256 bitmap to
stay crisp; a 64×64 source would be stretched ~4× and appear pixelated.

**Produce every new sprite at 1024×1024**, named `<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`, in
`src/sprites/`. The legacy `<Name>_64_x_64.png` files are superseded
thumbnails and are not read by the generator.

## Progress (2026-09-29)

The mapping/resolver/tooling + pending-aware drift guard landed on `dev` as
commit `4b80741` (full unit suite green): `src/card-art-map.json` is now
`version: 3`. Real coverage rose from **65 → 95 of 171** unique cards.

**Duplicate names split (commit `874f419`).** On producer decision Q8 the two
duplicate card names were renamed, so all **173 card names are now unique**:

- business `Florist` → **`Flower Shop`** — keeps the existing rose sprite
  (renamed `Flower Shop_1024_x_1024.png`); its `upgradePath` and
  `Upgrade to Garden Center`'s `targetBusiness` both follow.
- event `Community Garden` → **`Garden Party`** — now needs its own art and maps
  to the `Investment__` category until then.
- staff `Florist` keeps its name; its business restriction is now
  `Flower Shop|Commerce|Culture`.

Card IDs are intentionally unchanged (`biz-florist`, `evt-community-garden`) to
preserve save/challenge compatibility. After the split, **95 of 173** cards
resolve and **78** still render `Fallback`: the staff `Florist` and event
`Garden Party` joined the pending set, giving **46 distinct source sprites** to
produce.

## Desired change (confirmed strategy)

1. **Upgrades (39) — duplicate target art under the new display name.**
   For each `Upgrade to …`, copy the art of its `targetBusiness` to a new
   source sprite named after the upgrade's `newDisplayName` (all 39 are
   distinct, no collisions, and none is already a sprite). Seven targets are
   themselves gaps, so their art must be produced first: `Cafe`,
   `Health Kiosk`, `Laundromat`, `Library`, `Park`, `Playground`,
   `Town Fountain`.
2. **Business / community-space gaps (9) — new art.** `Laundromat`, `Cafe` and
   all community spaces except `Community Garden`: `Park`, `Library`,
   `Playground`, `Town Fountain`, `Health Kiosk`, `Community Shelter`,
   `Public Art`.
3. **Staff (25) — new staff art.** **One sprite per staff role** (confirmed
   2026-09-29), produced by the producer. The split moved `Florist` (staff)
   off the shared business sprite, so all 25 roles need art.
4. **Events (37) — category mapping.** Map each event to a category sprite
   keyed by `(trigger, targetSynergy)`; **unique (bespoke) art per category**
   (confirmed 2026-09-29), produced by the producer. `Garden Party` joined the
   category-mapped set after the split.
5. **Resolver / map.** Extend the generated mapping (and/or `CARD_ART_ALIASES`)
   so both consumers agree and regeneration stays deterministic; keep
   `Fallback` only as the genuine last resort.
6. **Drift guard.** Add a unit test over `card-data.csv` asserting full
   coverage and failing when a new art-less card appears.

## Required art (derived)

| Group | Cards | Mechanism | New sprites |
|-------|------:|-----------|------------:|
| Upgrade | 39 | Duplicate `targetBusiness` art under each upgrade's `newDisplayName` | 0 new (39 copies) |
| Business + community-space gaps | 9 | New source art | 9 |
| Staff | 25 | New source art — one per role | 25 |
| Event | 37 | Unique `(trigger × targetSynergy)` category art — 12 categories | 12 |
| **Total distinct source sprites** | | | **46** |

Event categories for the 36 missing events (representative = an event with
dedicated art today in the same category, available to duplicate):

| `trigger` | `targetSynergy` | Cards | Existing representative |
|-----------|-----------------|------:|-------------------------|
| Incident  | (none)          | 9 | Tax Audit |
| Incident  | Culture         | 1 | Cultural Grant |
| Incident  | Entertainment   | 1 | Noise Complaint |
| Incident  | Food            | 6 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Health          | 1 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Service         | 4 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| (none)          | 3 | Charity Drive |
| Investment| Commerce        | 1 | Grand Opening Sale |
| Investment| Entertainment   | 3 | Street Performer |
| Investment| Food            | 2 | Harvest Festival |
| Investment| Health          | 3 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| Service         | 2 | *(none — new)* |

Existing dedicated event art (35 events) is retained; only the 36 missing
events are category-mapped. **The producer confirmed on 2026-09-29 that each of
the 12 categories gets unique (bespoke) art** — the “existing representative”
column above is informational only and is not reused.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every **unique** card name in `card-data.csv` resolves via
   `MainStreetCardArt.hasDedicatedCardArt()` to a **non-`Fallback`** sprite
   (documented alias/category mapping counts); currently 65/171.
2. All 39 upgrade cards resolve to art duplicated from their `targetBusiness`
   under the upgrade's `newDisplayName`; no upgrade renders `Fallback`.
3. All 24 staff cards resolve to dedicated staff art; no staff card renders
   `Fallback`.
4. All 36 missing event cards resolve to a documented
   `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category sprite; no event card renders `Fallback`.
5. All 9 business / community-space gaps resolve to dedicated art; no card in
   either family renders `Fallback`.
6. A unit-test drift guard over `card-data.csv` asserts AC 1–5 and fails when a
   new card is added without art; `Fallback` remains in the map and resolver for
   genuinely-unknown/future cards (the existing "unknown card" test still passes).
7. Both consumers of `card-art-map.json` (runtime `MainStreetCardArt.ts` and
   `scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) apply the identical mapping;
   regeneration via `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` is
   deterministic and reproducible.
8. `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` and `public/assets/CREDITS.md`
   document the mapping rules and the licence/attribution of any new art.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
10. `npm run build` is green and the **full project test suite must pass** with
    the new changes.

## Constraints

- New art must be permissively licensed (CC0 / MIT / Apache 2.0) and attributed
  in `public/assets/CREDITS.md`.
- Source art remains `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`; `card-art-map.json`
  stays generated (never hand-edited).
- No change to the 64×64 zone geometry, the 140×80 card size, the 256×256
  embedded WebP format, or the SVG being self-contained (inline `data:` URI).
- Mapping logic must be expressed once and consumed by both the runtime and the
  static generator.

## Desired artefacts

- Up to 45 new `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` source files (9 business /
  community-space, 24 staff, up to 12 event categories) and 39 upgrade
  duplicates named by `newDisplayName`.
- Updated generated mapping + resolver.
- Drift-guard unit test in `tests/main-street/`.
- Docs + credits updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` — resolver: targetBusiness /
  category resolution or extended alias path.
- `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` — regenerated mapping (data).
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` —
  derive the upgrade-duplication and event-category mapping from
  `card-data.csv` + sprites.
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` —
  second consumer; mirror the mapping.
- `example-games/main-street/sprites/` — new + duplicated `_1024_x_1024.png`
  source art (producer).
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — add the `card-data.csv` drift guard.
- `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — document mapping rules.
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md` — licence/attribution for new art.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Art-availability dependency:** the resolver/tooling can land independently,
  but AC 1–5 cannot pass until the producer's sprites are committed. Plan
  should sequence tooling + drift guard first, art last.
- **Duplicate-name collision (resolved 2026-09-29):** the business `Florist`
  and the event `Community Garden` were renamed to `Flower Shop` and
  `Garden Party` (Q8), so every card name is now unique and no sprite is shared
  across families. IDs are unchanged for save/challenge compatibility.
- **Category-art fidelity (resolved 2026-09-29):** the producer confirmed
  unique (bespoke) art for all 12 event categories, so no representative
  sprite is reused.
- **Dual-consumer drift risk:** `generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` duplicates
  the alias logic; a mapping change that misses it silently diverges — assert
  both in tests.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "improve the existing 62 sprites" and "redesign the art
  zone" are out of scope — record separately if they surface.
- **Assumption:** `hasDedicatedCardArt()` remains name-keyed; any targetBusiness
  indirection is baked into the generated map so the public API is unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Changing the 64×64 left-art geometry or the 140×80 card dimensions.
- New card types or `card-data.csv` content changes (beyond `art_notes` if new
  art needs them).
- Filling the empty gameplay `description` column on the 45 `event` rows
  (unrelated to art; all 173 rows already carry `art_notes`).
- Redesigning/replacing the existing 62 dedicated sprites.
- Adding an in-repo image-generation tool (the producer supplies the art).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "Art scope / strategy: how much new art vs. mapping/reuse for the 108
  cards?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):** Option A — actively duplicate
  the current art using the new name; new art where necessary. Source:
  interactive producer reply.
- Q2 "Art production ownership & pipeline: who produces the new sprites, and
  does this item ship mapping machinery first?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-26):** "I will produce them." Source: interactive producer reply.
  Research: no in-repo sprite generator exists (last sprite commit
  `05026750`, external).
- Q3 "Event mapping granularity: what taxonomy, and is a category sprite
  acceptable for AC4?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):**
  `trigger` × `targetSynergy` categories. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q1 prior/open record superseded by the answers above (was OPEN QUESTION).
- Q4 "Source-art size: 64×64 or 1024×1024?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** the producer provides **1024×1024** source art; the 64×64 is
  the on-card display zone. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q5 "Staff art granularity: per-role or shared?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** **one sprite per role**. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q6 "Event-category art: reuse a representative or unique?" — **Answer
  (producer, 2026-09-29):** **unique** per category. Source: interactive
  producer reply.
- Q7 "Tighten the drift guard to strict zero-`Fallback` once art lands?" —
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-29):** **yes**. Source: interactive producer
  reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MP1QZC6Q005EMEZ** – Asset generation: placeholder SVGs for new cards (completed)
- **CG-0MLTFDAYD0J6KLY3** – Phaser Scene Static Card Layout (completed)

- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0mtorj5fs006b0un, acceptance, add, alias, apache (+136 more)

# Intake Brief: Serial Seller challenge (MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J)

**Headline:** Add a run-local **Serial Seller** challenge that completes when the player sells 3 or more street businesses in a single game, with live progress in the challenge HUD and a persistent Steam achievement consistent with the existing 12 challenges.

## Problem statement

Main Street's challenge pool currently has no goal that rewards _selling_ businesses, so the sell mechanic (Manage Card → Sell) is rarely a deliberate strategic path. This item adds a new run-local challenge, **Serial Seller**, that completes when the player sells 3 or more businesses in a single game, and shows live progress toward the goal in the challenge HUD.

## Users

- **Main Street players** choosing a strategy each run.
- **Main Street players** who need to gauge progress at a glance.
- **The designer/producer**, who wants the new challenge consistent with the existing challenge/achievement system.

Example user stories:

- As a Main Street player, I want a challenge that rewards selling businesses, so that a sell-and-reinvest strategy is a viable route to bonus points.
- As a player, I want to see my progress toward the challenge (e.g. "2/3 sold"), so I know how close I am to completing it.
- As the producer, I want the new challenge mapped to a persistent Steam achievement like the other 12 challenges, so the achievement set stays complete and consistent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- New challenge template and category: `ch-serial-seller` (title **Serial Seller**, description "Sell 3 or more businesses in a single game.") is added to `CHALLENGE_TEMPLATES` with `category: 'economic'` and `rewardPoints === CHALLENGE_BONUS_POINTS`; a new `economic` member is added to the `ChallengeCategory` union; its evaluator returns `true` iff the cumulative count of sold street businesses in the run is `>= 3`, and `false` on an empty grid.
- System integration and progress UI: the template participates in deterministic `selectChallenges` selection; completing it fires exactly once through `evaluateChallengesAfterAction` (bonus points awarded, activity-log entry written, persistent-achievement bridge invoked); the challenge HUD tracker renders live progress (e.g. `2/3`) for progress-capable challenges while challenges without progress metadata render unchanged.
- Undo/redo consistency: undoing a street sale reverts both the progress count and any challenge completion it caused; redo re-applies them exactly once (no double completion, no stale progress).
- Achievement mapping and cross-repo dependency: `ch-serial-seller` maps to achievement id `serial-seller` in `CHALLENGE_TO_ACHIEVEMENT_ID`; the blocking dependency work item (`MS-0MUOLL8W2004A3D7`, discovered-from this item) supplies the `core` submodule `electron/achievement-manifest.json` entry and the Steamworks backend API name (`TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER`); the achievement completeness/drift tests pass once the dependency has landed.
- Testing and validation: unit tests cover the evaluator (empty grid, 1/2/3 sales), selection inclusion, progress metadata, HUD progress rendering, and undo/redo.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Only street/tableau sales via the **Manage Card → Sell** dialog count (the `sellBusiness` path, tracked by `state.soldSlots`). Hand sales (`sellFromHand`) and the legacy `sellFromTableau` path are out of scope.
- **No new game-state field.** Reuse `state.soldSlots` (it is cumulative for the interactive path, because sold cards stay on the grid and cannot be closed) so save/load and command snapshots keep working unchanged.
- Existing tests assert **12** templates and category coverage for the 5 existing categories; these must be updated to 13 and (optionally) to assert `economic`. The category-coverage assertion for the original 5 categories must still hold.
- The achievement mapping is enforced by `tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts` against the launcher manifest, which lives in the **`core` git submodule (a separate repository)** — the manifest entry and Steamworks API name are handled by a separate **blocking dependency** work item `MS-0MUOLL8W2004A3D7` (producer/external action), not run-local.
- The per-run selection count (`config.challengesPerRun`, default 3) and the end-of-game scoring formula are unchanged — only the template pool grows.
- The progress indicator must fit the existing challenge panel geometry (compact single-line rows); avoid layout regressions.
- All written output in UK English.

## Existing state

- `src/MainStreetChallenges.ts` defines the `ChallengeCategory` union (`synergy`, `placement`, `resource`, `upgrade`, `cross-cutting`), 12 `CHALLENGE_TEMPLATES`, `DEFAULT_CHALLENGES_PER_RUN = 3`, and `selectChallenges`/`evaluateChallenges` wrappers over the generic `@core-engine` challenge API. Evaluators are pure functions of `MainStreetState`. Selection is seeded from `config.challengesPerRun` in `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts`.
- Challenge evaluation runs after every action (`evaluateChallengesAfterAction`) and at end of turn; completions are non-revocable during a run but are captured/restored by command snapshots (`captureSnapshot`/`restoreSnapshot` in `src/MainStreetCommands.ts`, which include `soldSlots`, `challengesCompleted`, and per-challenge completion flags).
- `state.soldSlots: boolean[]` marks sold street cards; sold cards remain on the grid as inert synergy anchors and cannot be closed, so the true-count is monotonic for the interactive path and is captured in undo snapshots.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` (`refreshChallengeTracker`) renders the challenge panel as compact rows: indicator + title + description, with a `Challenges (n/N)` header. There is currently no per-challenge progress display.
- `src/MainStreetAchievements.ts` maps every challenge template 1:1 to a persistent Steam achievement; `tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts` guards completeness and drift against `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json`.

## Desired change

- Add an `economic` challenge category and the `ch-serial-seller` template with an evaluator counting sold street businesses and an optional progress provider.
- Add an optional `progress?: (state: MainStreetState) => { current: number; target: number }` field to the `Challenge` interface and render it in the challenge HUD tracker (e.g. `2/3`), leaving progress-less challenges visually unchanged.
- Add the `serial-seller` achievement mapping and create the blocking dependency work item for the `core` manifest entry + Steamworks API name.
- Update the affected tests (template count, evaluator/selection/progress/undo, achievement mapping) and documentation.

Design note: keeping progress as an **optional Main Street-specific** field on `Challenge` (rather than extending the generic `ChallengeDefinition<TState>` in `@core-engine`) keeps the change surgical and avoids touching the core engine. If a second progress-capable challenge is added later, promoting the field to the generic interface can be revisited.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetChallenges.ts` — add `economic` to `ChallengeCategory`, add optional `progress` to `Challenge`, add the `ch-serial-seller` template (evaluator + progress).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` — render progress in `refreshChallengeTracker`.
- `src/MainStreetAchievements.ts` — add `'ch-serial-seller': 'serial-seller'` to `CHALLENGE_TO_ACHIEVEMENT_ID`.
- `tests/main-street/challenges.test.ts` — update template count (12 → 13); add evaluator, selection, and progress-metadata tests.
- `tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts` — mapping completeness/drift now includes `serial-seller` (green once the child manifest entry lands).
- `tests/main-street/` challenge-HUD/scene test — add progress-rendering coverage (extend an existing scene/HUD test or add a focused one).
- `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json` — **blocking dependency** `MS-0MUOLL8W2004A3D7` (core submodule): add the `serial-seller` entry with `TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER`.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` and/or `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — document the new challenge/category if the challenge catalogue is described there.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — only if the progress indicator requires a layout constant tweak (avoid if possible).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Cross-repo achievement dependency (blocking, build impact).** The manifest lives in the `core` submodule and the drift guard (`tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts`) fails the build until the dependency (`MS-0MUOLL8W2004A3D7`) lands and the submodule pointer is bumped. Sequence the dependency first; this item must not reach `in_review` ahead of it.
- **Test friction from template count.** Several tests derive from `CHALLENGE_TEMPLATES.length`; only `challenges.test.ts` hardcodes 12. Keep the category-coverage list at the original 5 so `economic` is not required to have ≥2 templates (scope creep risk — do not add a second economic challenge here; capture as a separate linked work item).
- **Undo semantics.** Because completion is flagged on the `ActiveChallenge` and also recorded in `challengesCompleted`, redo must not double-add. Existing per-action reset (`completedChallengeIds.length = 0`) already guards this; add regression coverage.
- **Progress layout.** The challenge rows are compact; a progress suffix must not overlap the description column. Verify at the shipping HUD width.
- **Assumption:** `soldSlots` true-count is the intended "businesses sold" metric (confirmed by producer, Q6 = a). If a future non-street sell path should count, a state counter will be needed — out of scope.
- **Assumption:** final player-facing text is title **Serial Seller** and description "Sell 3 or more businesses in a single game." (producer-confirmed Q7 update); the `economic` category keeps the original 5-category coverage assertions intact.
- **Scope-creep risk:** adding more economic challenges, changing reward points, adding new achievement art, or counting hand/legacy sells are out of scope; capture as linked work items.

## Related work

- `MS-0MUNO0M2I004TK04` (`Wire Main Street challenges to Steam achievements`, stage `plan_complete`) / `CG-0MUNC7FK5001T5CP` — established the 1:1 challenge→achievement mapping and drift guard this item extends.
- `CG-0MU37CKRR008252I` — per-action challenge evaluation (the path that completes this challenge after a sell).
- `CG-0MTCP7F9S009HARC` / `CG-0MT5XT7K3005IBBV` — Sell vs Close mechanics (sold markers, undo snapshot/restore).
- `MS-0MUMAZTAY00515MC` (`Main Street: verify capacity-stable HandView slots (bump core submodule …)`, completed/`in_review`) — precedent for bumping the `core` submodule pointer from a Main Street change, as the blocking dependency here will need to do.

# Storyline Coverage Analytics in Monte Carlo Harness

## Problem Statement

The Monte Carlo balance harness (MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts) currently tracks card ownership, market offers, and economy history across simulation runs, but has no visibility into storyline event coverage. Storyline events — which form branching chains with accept/reject choices — are a key game mechanic, yet the harness cannot report how often storylines fire, how deeply their chains progress, whether cycles appear, or what impact storyline choices have on win rates. This leaves the balance team blind to storyline-related balance issues.

## Users

- **Balance team / game designers**: Want to understand whether storylines are contributing positively to the game (e.g., do "Accept" choices correlate with higher win rates? Do certain storylines trigger too or too rarely?).
- **Content designers**: Want to verify that all storylines are being exercised in simulation and that chains progress reasonably (not dead-ending too quickly or cycling excessively).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Storyline fire frequency**: The harness reports how many runs and what percentage feature each storyline (`storyline-economy`, `storyline-health`, `storyline-labor`, `storyline-restaurant`, `storyline-tax`), derived from event-choice transcript records captured during simulation runs.

2. **Chain depth tracking**: For each storyline event encountered, the harness tracks how far the chain progresses (number of consecutive chain cards pushed), reported per storyline as a distribution (mean, median, max depth) across runs.

3. **Cycle detection**: The harness detects and counts cycle occurrences (tax → tax-error → tax-inquiry → tax, per `storyline-manifest.json` edges with `cycle: true`), reporting cycle frequency per storyline and per run.

4. **Win-rate impact of choices**: For each storyline with choices (flu-outbreak, popular-menu, recession, strike-service, tax, tax-error, tax-inquiry), the harness computes the win-rate differential between "Accept" and "Reject" choices — similar to existing M2 win-rate delta pattern.

5. **Integration with existing analytics**: Storyline analytics are exposed as new functions in the balance engine (`src/scripts/balance/engine/`) following the same pattern as existing metrics (G1–G8, M1–M7), with graceful degradation when storyline data is absent.

## Constraints

- **Non-blocking**: This is a deferred enhancement; it must not change existing Monte Carlo harness behaviour (strategies, termination, output format for non-storyline fields).
- **Graceful degradation**: All new storyline metrics return `null` when event-choice data is not available in run summaries (consistent with existing M4/M6/G4/G6/G7 patterns).
- **Builds on existing transcript recording**: The harness already has a lazy `recordMainStreetEvent` call path via `require('./MainStreetTranscript')`; the extension should extend this path to capture event-choice data into a new field on `MonteCarloRunSummary`.
- **No UI changes required**: Output is analytical (JSON/CSV), consistent with existing harness output.

## Existing State

- Monte Carlo harness (`MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts`) runs simulations with strategies (market-greedy, demo-greedy, greedy, banking-greedy, random) and records `MonteCarloRunSummary` per seed.
- The harness already records `cardsOwned`, `marketOffers`, and `economyHistory` on run summaries (Phase 1 data).
- Storyline events with choices are resolved in-engine; `recordStorylineResolution` in `MainStreetStoryline.ts` emits `event-choice` transcript events.
- The Monte Carlo harness has a try/catch wrapper for `recordMainStreetEvent` that silently ignores failures when no recorder is wired.
- Storyline manifest (`docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json`) defines 5 storylines, 14 edge transitions, and 1 cycle group.
- Balance engine (`src/scripts/balance/engine/`) has 8 global metrics (G1–G8) and 7 card metrics (M1–M7) with graceful degradation patterns.

## Desired Change

1. **Extend `MonteCarloRunSummary`** with a new field capturing event choices encountered during a run (event ID, choice made, chain depth at that point).
2. **Wire transcript recording** in the Monte Carlo harness so that event-choice events are captured (not just ai-action events).
3. **Add storyline analytics functions** to the balance engine:
   - `computeStorylineFireFrequency(runs)`: percentage of runs per storyline.
   - `computeChainDepthStats(runs)`: depth distribution per storyline.
   - `computeCycleStats(runs)`: cycle frequency per storyline and per run.
   - `computeChoiceWinRateDelta(runs, eventId)`: win-rate difference between Accept vs Reject.
4. **Export storyline metrics** from the balance engine barrel file.
5. **Add tests** covering all new analytics functions.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — Extend `MonteCarloRunSummary` interface; wire transcript recording for event-choice events.
- `src/scripts/balance/engine/index.ts` — Barrel file for new storyline metrics exports.
- `src/scripts/balance/engine/storyline-metrics.ts` (new) — New analytics module for storyline-specific metrics.
- `tests/main-street/balance/storyline-metrics.test.ts` (new) — Tests for storyline analytics functions.
- `docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json` — Reference for storyline definitions and cycle edges (read-only).

## Related Work

- **MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV** — write storylines (epic, completed): The parent epic that shipped the storyline system.
- **MS-0MUMP94S7008KTI0** — Storyline graph/manifest export & JSON schema (completed): Provides the manifest data model.
- **MS-0MUMP96XH002SJ89** — Named storylines, outcome feedback & continuity indicator (completed): Provides storyline naming and feedback mechanics.
- **MS-0MUMP944B009PEO6** — Static validator & npm gate (completed): Validates storyline integrity.

# Extend storyline options with conditional and cost-gated effects

## Problem statement

The generalised storyline option model (`StorylineOption`) currently supports
only a label, a single successor, and an apply/skip effect policy. Content and
engine authors cannot express options that are only available when the player
can afford them, that branch to different successors based on game state, or
that carry their own extra effects. The game-agnostic seam
(`src/MainStreetStoryline.ts`) was explicitly designed to grow into these
semantics, and this capability was deliberately deferred from the
`write-storylines` epic as speculative until now.

## Users

- **Engine/content authors** — need richer per-option semantics (affordability
  gates, state-based branching, extra effects) without bypassing the
  game-agnostic seam or hand-writing bespoke engine code per card.
- **TCE / Main Street developers** — need the extension to stay declarative,
  serialisable, statically validatable, and portable to the core engine.
- **Players** — should only be offered choices they can actually take, and
  should have their decisions reflected accurately in coins/reputation.
- **AI / Monte Carlo** — must keep selecting legal, presented options so
  headless games never stall or pick a hidden/unaffordable branch.

### Example user stories

- "As an engine author, I want to gate an option behind a coin/reputation cost,
  so the choice only appears when the player can afford it."
- "As a content designer, I want an option's successor to depend on coins or
  reputation, so one choice can lead down different branches."
- "As a content designer, I want an option to apply an extra effect on top of
  its apply/skip policy, so choices can have their own consequences."
- "As a developer, I want invalid cost/condition data to fail the validator, so
  mis-authored storylines cannot ship."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Backwards-compatible model extension.** `StorylineOption` gains optional
   `cost`, `extraEffect` (`{ coins?: number; reputation?: number }`), and
   ordered `conditionalSuccessors` (`{ when: { field: 'coins'|'reputation';
   op: '>='|'<='|'>'|'<'|'=='; value: number }; successorId }`) fields. Omitting
   all three preserves today's behaviour exactly — verified by the existing
   legacy-equivalence and C1 regression harness passing unchanged.
   *Metric: unit tests + existing regression harness pass with zero behavioural deltas.*

- **Cost gating.** An option whose `cost` exceeds the player's current
   coins/reputation is **omitted** from the presented option list; available
   options are computed and stored with the pending choice so resolution
   indexing, transcript tokens, and save/load stay stable. Selecting an
   affordable option deducts the declared cost as an additional payment,
   independent of its `effectPolicy`, and applies any `extraEffect`.
   *Metric: unit tests assert exact coin/reputation deltas, omission, and stable indexing.*

- **Conditional successors.** `conditionalSuccessors` is evaluated in order;
   the first matching rule wins, and the option's `successorId` is the fallback
   when none match. Above/below threshold, equality boundary, and no-match
   fallback cases are covered, including succeeding-card push.
   *Metric: unit tests for each boundary/fallback case.*

- **Static validation & schema.** The validator and manifest schema reject
   invalid new data — negative/empty cost, malformed conditions (unknown field
   or op, non-numeric value), and dangling conditional successors — while the
   shipped CSVs validate cleanly and the doc-drift test passes.
   *Metric: validator unit tests with broken fixtures + clean run on shipped content.*

- **AI / Monte Carlo integration.** `decideEventChoice` (and the generalised
   AI selection path) chooses only among presented/affordable options and
   accounts for cost/extra-effect deltas; the regression and Monte Carlo
   harnesses run to completion without stalls.
   *Metric: AI policy tests + regression/Monte Carlo harness green.*

- **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes — `docs/main-street/storylines.md` (option model, resolution
   lifecycle, roadmap), the migration notes in `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts`,
   and the CSV column reference in `src/README.md` (confirming the new
   semantics remain programmatic, not CSV-authored).
   *Metric: doc-drift test passes; reviewer confirms docs match code.*

- **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.
   *Metric: full test suite green.*

## Constraints

- **Programmatic authoring only (producer decision Q1=A).** Extend the
  in-memory model, engine resolution, validator, and schema. Keep the legacy
  CSV at the two-way Accept/Reject shape; do **not** add CSV columns for the
  new semantics.
- **Declarative and serialisable (producer decision Q3=A).** Only
  field/op/value conditions and numeric deltas. Arbitrary callbacks are out of
  scope here — see the follow-up work item below.
- **Game-agnostic seam.** New semantics must live behind
  `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` and keep the future core-engine extraction
  viable (pure/declarative data, no Main-Street globals baked in beyond the
  injected template registry).
- **Affordability is coins and/or reputation (producer decision Q2.1).** A cost
  may specify either or both; an option is available only when *all* specified
  costs are affordable.
- **Omit, do not disable (producer decision Q2.2).** Unaffordable options are
  removed from the presented list, not shown greyed out.
- **Cost is a real payment (producer decision Q2.3).** Deducted from the
  player in addition to the option's apply/skip effect policy.
- No shipped card content is expected to use the new semantics; existing
  gameplay must remain byte-for-byte equivalent.

## Existing state

- `StorylineOption` (`src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts`) = `{ label, successorId,
  effectPolicy }`. `CompiledStoryline` wraps an ordered option list.
- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` compiles legacy `hasChoices` /
  `acceptNextCardId` / `rejectNextCardId` into `[Accept, Reject]`, and supports
  explicit multi-way lists via `registerStorylineOptions(eventId, options)`.
  `getStorylineOptions(event)` is pure (no state) and is used by callers,
  the validator, and the graph exporter.
- `resolveStorylineOption(state, event, option)`
  (`src/MainStreetStoryline.ts`) applies `effectPolicy` and pushes
  `option.successorId`; `resolveEventOption(state, optionIndex)`
  (`src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`) indexes the option list, records the
  transcript, and drives `pushChainCard`.
- `decideEventChoice` (`src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts`) returns a binary
  `'accept' | 'reject'` and reasons about `coinDelta` / `reputationDelta`,
  `projectEventCoinDelta`, `eventSeverity`, and successor severity.
- Validation lives in `src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts`; the manifest/schema
  in `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` and
  `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json`; docs in
  `docs/main-street/storylines.md` (§2 model, §3 lifecycle, §9 seam, §10
  roadmap).
- `PendingEventChoice` (`src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts`) currently stores
  `{ event, chosenOption, resolved }`.

## Desired change

Extend the option model and resolution path so that:

1. Options declare an optional affordability `cost`; the presented option list
   is filtered to affordable options before the dialog/AI sees it, and the
   filtered list is stored with the pending choice.
2. Options declare an optional `extraEffect` and ordered
   `conditionalSuccessors`, both applied/selected at resolution time using the
   declarative predicate vocabulary.
3. Selection deducts `cost`, applies `extraEffect` independently of
   `effectPolicy`, and pushes the first matching conditional successor (or the
   default `successorId`).
4. The validator, schema, and graph/manifest export understand the new fields;
   the AI policy operates over the presented option list.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — Extend `StorylineOption` with `cost`,
  `extraEffect`, and `conditionalSuccessors`; add a `Condition` type.
- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` — Filter options by affordability, apply cost +
  extra effects, resolve conditional successors; expose a state-aware
  accessibility accessor alongside the pure `getStorylineOptions`.
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — Store the presented/available option list on
  `PendingEventChoice` so indexing and save/load remain stable.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — `resolveEventOption` uses the stored
  presented list; update logging/transcript for cost and extra effects.
- `src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts` — `decideEventChoice` selects only among
  presented options and accounts for cost/extra-effect deltas.
- `src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts` — Validate cost/condition/effect data and
  conditional successor targets.
- `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` + `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json`
  — Represent and validate the new option metadata in the manifest/graph.
- `docs/main-street/storylines.md` — Document the extended option model and
  resolution semantics; update the seam/migration notes.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-model.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/validate-storylines.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/storyline-graph.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts` — New/extended coverage.

## Related work

- `MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV` — **write storylines** (completed epic; parent context).
- `MS-0MUMP93DI0018OGV` — **Storyline model & extraction seam** (completed; the
  generalised `StorylineOption` this extends).
- `MS-0MUMP92O9002772U` — **Storyline behaviour regression harness** (completed;
  the byte-for-byte regression guard).
- `MS-0MUMP944B009PEO6` — **Static validator & npm gate** (completed; the
  validator this extends).
- `MS-0MUMP95IW002ARWJ` — **Storyline authoring helper CLI** (completed).
- `MS-0MUMP94S7008KTI0` — **Storyline graph/manifest export & JSON schema**
  (completed; manifest/schema this extends).
- `MS-0MUPORT1Z000QX8N` — **Support arbitrary callback conditions/successors in
  storyline options** (follow-up, medium priority, `discovered-from` this item).
- Roadmap entry: `docs/main-street/storylines.md` §10.

## Risks

- **Option-index drift.** Filtering options changes the index space; the
  pending-choice list must be frozen at draw time or the UI, AI, and transcript
  can disagree. *Mitigation:* store the presented list on
  `PendingEventChoice` and resolve by index into it.
- **AI divergence.** `decideEventChoice` is currently binary; a generalised
  selector that ignores affordability/cost could pick a hidden option or stall.
  *Mitigation:* route AI through the same presented list; cover with
  regression/Monte Carlo tests.
- **Manifest/schema churn.** Adding optional fields can break the graph export
  or doc-drift test. *Mitigation:* keep new fields optional and update schema,
  exporter, and docs in the same change.
- **Scope creep.** Arbitrary callbacks, CSV authoring, and per-option animation
  are explicitly out of scope; the callback escape hatch is tracked separately
  as `MS-0MUPORT1Z000QX8N`.

---

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Delivery surface.** How far should this change reach?
  - Answer (producer): **A** — extend the in-memory model + engine resolution +
    validator/schema only, programmatically via `registerStorylineOptions`;
    keep the legacy CSV at two-way Accept/Reject. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 — Cost-gated semantics.**
  1. What gates eligibility?
     - Answer (producer): **coins and/or reputation**. Source: interactive reply.
  2. When unaffordable, omitted or shown disabled?
     - Answer (producer): **omitted**. Source: interactive reply.
  3. Is the cost deducted on selection in addition to apply/skip?
     - Answer (producer): **yes**. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 — Conditional successors & per-option extra effects representation.**
  - Answer (producer): **A** — declarative, serialisable data
    (`extraEffect` + ordered `{ when, successorId }` rules with `successorId`
    fallback). Additionally: create a **medium-priority follow-up work item**
    to add arbitrary callbacks. Source: interactive reply. Follow-up created as
    `MS-0MUPORT1Z000QX8N`.

### Assumptions

- No shipped card content is expected to use the new semantics; existing
  legacy/card behaviour must remain byte-for-byte equivalent.
- Because a pending choice blocks all player actions, the set of affordable
  options is stable between draw and resolution; storing the presented list on
  the pending choice makes this explicit and save/load-safe.
- Cost deduction that drops coins or reputation to zero triggers the normal
  loss checks (no special-casing).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUO8B93V002CL06** – Help panel content drifts from PRD milestone 5 (7 sections, >8 lines) (in-progress)
- **MS-0MUOSII720060IZQ** – Implement free market re-roll mechanic (engine + state + bias draw) (blocked)

# Intake Brief: Visual storyline authoring editor

**Epic.** Producer decisions (2026-10-01, interactive reply): **Q1 = A (in-repo
local web tool)**; **Q2 = A (epic, decomposed into vertical slices)**;
**Q3 = A (curated form/guided editor)**.

## Problem statement

Storylines can only be authored today by hand-editing `src/card-data.csv` or by
driving the transaction-safe `storyline-author` CLI, and the graph can only be
viewed as a generated Mermaid/JSON artefact. Content designers therefore cannot
*see* the arc they are editing, cannot discover links and dangling targets
visually, and cannot make a guided, validated edit in one place. The seed
roadmap entry (`docs/main-street/storylines.md` §10) calls for a visual
storyline authoring editor that reads `docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json`,
renders the graph interactively, and writes edits back through the same
transactional, self-validating author operations.

## Users

- **Content designers / producers** — see a storyline's shape at a glance,
  inspect a card's links and metadata, and make guided edits (rename, retarget a
  link, regroup a storyline, add a card) without touching CSV internals.
- **TCE / Main Street developers** — trust that every edit goes through one
  validated, transactional write path and that committed artefacts stay in sync
  with `src/card-data.csv`.
- **Future tooling authors** — reuse an editor/view-model seam that reads the
  manifest rather than re-parsing the CSV.

### Example user stories

- "As a content designer, I want to open a local tool, see the storyline graph
  rendered from the manifest, and click a card to inspect its links, so I can
  understand an arc before changing it."
- "As a content designer, I want to edit a card's name, effect and successor
  links in a form and see a preview plus validation errors, so I cannot write
  a dangling chain."
- "As a content designer, I want the committed graph and manifest regenerated
  automatically after an accepted edit, so the docs never drift from content."
- "As a developer, I want the editor to be a local dev tool that is excluded
  from the game build and reuses the existing author API, so it adds no runtime
  dependency and no second CSV write path."

## Scope areas

### A. Editor host and read-only graph viewer

1. A local web tool launched with `npm run storylines:editor` from the repo
   root, built on the existing Vite/`vite-node` toolchain (no new runtime
   dependency). It is a development tool and must not be included in the game
   build.
2. An interactive, manifest-driven graph view: storyline grouping, choice cards
   distinguished from plain incidents, cycle edges marked, pan/zoom and
   node selection. Read-only in the first slice.

### B. Transactional write bridge

3. A Node-side bridge that exposes the existing author operations
   (`add-card`, `link`, `set-storyline` from `src/scripts/storyline-author.ts`)
   and the validator (`src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts`) to the editor.
4. Every edit is **previewed and validated before writing**; an invalid result
   leaves `src/card-data.csv` untouched and surfaces actionable errors.
5. On an accepted edit, regenerate `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd` and
   `docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json` via the existing
   `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` generator so the existing drift test stays
   green.
6. Concurrency guard: refuse to overwrite the CSV if it changed on disk outside
   the editor session (content hash / mtime check) and ask the author to reload.

### C. Curated form/guided editing UX

7. Edit an existing card's fields: name, effect text, coin/reputation deltas,
   `hasChoices`, `acceptNextCardId`, `rejectNextCardId`, `storylineId`,
   `storylineTitle`.
8. Add a new card and link it into a storyline through a guided form; discard
   pending (unwritten) changes before committing.

### D. Storyline management, docs and tests

9. Storyline-level operations (create/rename a `storylineId`/`storylineTitle`
   group and reassign member cards) driven through the same author API.
10. Documentation in `docs/main-street/storylines.md` (and the `src/README.md`
    script/column references) covering launch, the viewer, the edit workflow,
    validation and artefact regeneration.
11. Unit tests for the view-model/API bridge and a browser (Playwright) test
    for the viewer and a representative edit round-trip.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Editor launches locally** — `npm run storylines:editor` starts the tool
   from the repo root on the existing Vite/`vite-node` toolchain with no new
   runtime dependency; the command is documented in `docs/main-street/storylines.md`.
   Verified by a test that invokes the entry point (dry/`--help` mode) and asserts
   it exits 0.
2. **Manifest-driven interactive graph** — the editor renders the committed
   manifest (`docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json`): all nodes and edges
   appear, choice cards are visually distinct, storyline grouping and cycle
   edges are shown, and selecting a node shows its links/metadata. Covered by a
   browser test.
3. **Read-only fidelity** — the editor's view model (nodes, edges, storyline
   ids/titles, cycle flags) matches the committed manifest exactly; verified by
   a unit test that diffs the view model against the manifest and the JSON
   schema.
4. **Curated editing via the author API only** — the editor can edit the fields

# Fix stale `example-games/main-street/` paths in docs after the `src/` migration

**Headline.** The game repo's docs still point at the pre-migration `example-games/main-street/` layout; remap every remaining reference under `docs/` to `src/`, reword the one migration-plan sentence that must name the old layout, and add a Vitest guard that fails if the stale prefix is ever reintroduced.

## Problem statement

The Main Street source tree moved from `example-games/main-street/` to `src/`, but 33 references across 10 files under `docs/` still use the old prefix. Anyone following a doc link or command ends up at a path that no longer exists, and there is no test preventing further drift.

## Users

- **Game developer / maintainer** — follows a doc reference (e.g. `docs/main-street/tutorial-localization.md`) and needs it to resolve to the current `src/` file.
- **Agent / tooling** — greps or links against docs and must not be sent to dead paths.

Example user stories:

- As a maintainer reading `docs/main-street/tutorial-localization.md`, I want its file links to resolve so I can jump straight to `src/TutorialFlow.ts`.
- As a reviewer, I want a failing test when someone re-adds an `example-games/main-street/` reference to `docs/`, so the migration cannot regress.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Zero stale references** — the substring `example-games/main-street/` does not appear anywhere under `docs/` (all file types, including `docs/main-street/card-catalog-baseline.json`).
2. **Migration sentence reworded** — `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-6.md` §2 "File-level migration plan from … to `src/*`" is reworded to name the legacy layout without the literal `example-games/main-street/` prefix (no allowlist is introduced).
3. **Remap targets verified** — each remapped reference resolves to its `src/` target where the target exists; line-number suffixes are preserved (e.g. `src/MainStreetState.ts:217-224`) and illustrative not-yet-created filenames keep their new-layout prefix (e.g. `src/i18n/tutorial-fr.csv`).
4. **Drift guard** — a Vitest test under `tests/main-street/` recursively scans `docs/` for `example-games/main-street/` and fails on any match; it includes a negative case proving it detects an injected reference.
5. **Docs updated** — all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Scope is the game repo's own `docs/` tree only. The `core/` git submodule (separate `Tableau-Card-Engine` repo, ~48 refs) is **out of scope**.
- No allowlist: the producer chose to reword the migration-plan sentence rather than exempt files, so the guard is zero-tolerance.
- Mechanical remap only — no reflowing or rewriting doc prose beyond the single required reword.
- CHANGELOG.md is excluded (managed by the ship release pipeline).

## Existing state

- 32 stale refs across 9 `docs/main-street/*.md` files, plus 1 in `docs/main-street/card-catalog-baseline.json`:
  - `playtest-scenarios.md` (2), `prd-balance-process-and-tooling.md` (3), `prd-milestone-1.md` (2), `prd-milestone-2.md` (3), `prd-milestone-3.md` (9), `prd-milestone-4.md` (1), `prd-milestone-6.md` (13), `specialization-skills.md` (1), `tutorial-localization.md` (17), `card-dimensions.md` (1), `card-catalog-baseline.json` (1).

- All remap targets exist in `src/` except: (a) `MainStreetState.ts:217-224` (line-number suffix, target exists), (b) `i18n/tutorial-fr.csv` / `tutorial-fr.ts` (illustrative new-file names in the localisation how-to), and (c) the extensionless `../../src/i18n/tutorial-en` import example.
- Precedent for a docs guard: `tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts` (Vitest, scans a doc and its links).

## Desired change

1. Mechanically replace `example-games/main-street/` → `src/` in every in-scope doc, preserving any `:line` suffix and relative-import `../` prefixes.
2. Reword `prd-milestone-6.md` §2's migration-plan sentence so it no longer contains the literal old prefix.
3. Update `card-catalog-baseline.json`'s `source` metadata to point at `src/MainStreetTiers.ts`.
4. Add `tests/main-street/docs-path-drift.test.ts`: recursively read every file under `docs/`, assert none contains `example-games/main-street/`, and include a negative test that injects the string and asserts detection.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-6.md` — reword §2 migration-plan line; remap the 11 file-list refs.
- `docs/main-street/tutorial-localization.md` — 17 refs (links, import examples, tables, how-to steps).

- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-4.md` — 1 ref (`git log --` example path).

The five-turn payback rebalance (MS-0MUQ50I1Y000B6L3, producer decision Q3 = C) deliberately tightened the economy, making net liquidity slack and run length short; it was left open whether difficulty should now be expressed through `winThreshold` / run length rather than income. On 2026-10-09 the producer reviewed refreshed canonical-profile evidence and confirmed the current state is acceptable: **no change** to `winThreshold` or `maxTurns`.

## Users

- **Producer / game designer** — owns the difficulty-intent decision.
- **Balance engineer** — needs the decision recorded with reproducible evidence and a stable baseline.
- **Future maintainer** — needs to know the current presets are intentional, so they are not "fixed" without new data.

Example user stories:

- As the **producer**, I want the difficulty-lever decision recorded with evidence, so the design intent is explicit and auditable.
- As a **balance engineer**, I want the accepted win-rate ladder and run-length baseline documented, so I do not re-open the question without new data.
- As a **future maintainer**, I want the unchanged presets and the existing guard tests documented as deliberate, so an accidental change is caught.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The producer decision is recorded on the work item and in the balance docs: **no change** to per-difficulty `winThreshold` (Easy 10,000 / Medium 12,000 / Hard 15,000) and **no `maxTurns` cap** added, together with the rationale and the canonical-profile evidence it is based on (comment `MS-C0MV1D0IBA001ROOU`).
2. `docs/main-street/further-balancing-recommendations.md` §5 R3 is updated to mark the recommendation **confirmed / no change**, with the current measured metrics and a link to the decision.
3. The decision is documented where the presets are defined (`src/MainStreetDifficulty.ts` preset comment) and/or in `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md`, so the unchanged presets read as intentional rather than unexamined.
4. **Validation:** re-run the canonical 200-seed / 60-turn greedy profile and confirm the win-rate ladder holds (Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard) and each difficulty is within its PRD band; confirm the existing guard tests (`tests/main-street/difficulty-presets.test.ts` — pins `winThreshold` values and that `maxTurns` is `undefined`; `tests/main-street/monte-carlo-greedy-guardrail.test.ts` — pins the win-rate bands and ladder) still pass.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No preset value changes** — `winThreshold` values are unchanged and no `maxTurns` is added (producer decision A, 2026-10-09).
- **No engine-rule changes** — score formula, action economy and synergy formula are out of scope per the parent's non-recommendations.
- **Preserve the primary balance gate** — a monotone-decreasing win-rate ladder `Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard`.
- **Canonical profile is fixed** — 200 seeds `mc-balance-0…199`, harness `maxTurns` 60, strategy `greedy`, all three difficulties.

- `avgTurns_greedy_medium` informational band is **14–22** (`src/scripts/balance/guards/thresholds.ts`); PRD Milestone 1 describes the intended game as "surviving 20 turns". Run length remains below that intent, but the producer accepted this.

- **Documentation/decision-only.** No source behaviour change, no preset change.
- Update the R3 recommendation row and the difficulty/balance documentation to record the confirmation, the refreshed evidence and the "no change" rationale.
- Confirm (not add) that the existing guard tests encode the decision; re-run the canonical profile to reconfirm the ladder.

# Resolve conditional successors at option resolution time

## Summary

When resolving an option, evaluate `conditionalSuccessors` in order — the first matching rule wins. Fall back to the option's existing `successorId` when no conditions match. This enables branching based on game state.

- **Conditional evaluation.** `conditionalSuccessors` are evaluated sequentially; the first rule whose `{ field, op, value }` matches current `state.resourceBank.{field}` determines the pushed card ID.

# Intake Brief — Credit AI challenge completions to the AI seat (MS-0MUWNTJIK009O6BZ)

## Problem statement

In competitive (human-vs-AI) play the challenge (meta-goal) system is
**run-global**: `state.activeChallenges` / `state.challengesCompleted` are a
single shared pool, and challenge evaluation runs after *every* action —
human **or** AI. As a result, when an AI seat's action satisfies a challenge,
the challenge is marked complete, its bonus points are added to **every**
seat's score (including the human's), the human's HUD/celebration shows it,
and the human's Steam achievement is unlocked. The player is therefore
credited with the AI's challenges.

## Users

- **Human player in competitive mode** — wants challenge credit to reflect
  who actually completed the challenge.
  - *As a competitive player, I want a challenge completed by an AI opponent
    to be credited to that AI, so that my score, achievements and Game Over
    summary only reflect my own challenge completions.*
- **AI opponent seat** — should receive (and be shown as receiving) the
  challenge bonus for challenges it completes.
- **Single-player player** — must be unaffected; challenges stay run-global.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Per-seat attribution.** In competitive mode each challenge completion
   records the seat that performed the completing action
   (`ActiveChallenge.completedBySeatId`, or an equivalent per-seat completion
   map). Single-player / legacy runs without seat context retain the current
   global attribution.
2. **Exclusive credit.** Only one player can achieve each challenge: once a
   challenge is completed by a seat it is never re-completed or re-credited to
   another seat.
3. **Per-seat scoring.** `updateCompetitiveScores` awards
   `challengeBonusPoints` **only** for challenges completed by that seat — no
   seat is credited with another seat's completion.
4. **Per-seat UI and achievements.** The Game Over summary presents a
   **per-seat** challenge breakdown (who completed which challenge) rather than
   a single run-global list; in competitive mode the challenge celebration and
   HUD show only the human seat's completions, and the Steam achievement bridge
   fires only for challenges completed by the human seat. Single-player
   presentation is unchanged.
5. **Consistency and persistence.** Attribution holds across the per-action and
   end-of-turn EndCheck evaluation paths, undo, save/load, and headless
   (Monte Carlo) play.
6. **Testing.** Tests cover per-seat attribution, per-seat scoring, the
   per-seat Game Over summary, celebration/achievement gating, and save/load.
7. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs
   site entries.
8. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Competitive mode is human vs one-or-more AI seats on a shared,
  owner-tagged street; challenge evaluators read the shared `streetGrid`.
- `challengeBonusPoints` is difficulty-scaled (Easy 1500 / Medium 1000 /
  Hard 800) and feeds `computeScore` / `updateCompetitiveScores`.
- The end-of-turn EndCheck remains a safety net for closing-phase
  completions; attribution must survive both the per-action and EndCheck
  evaluation paths.
- Save/load must tolerate legacy saves with no attribution data (treated as
  global/single-player).
- CHANGELOG.md is excluded (managed by the ship pipeline); no CI/CD pipeline
  tests.

## Existing state

- `src/MainStreetChallenges.ts` — `ActiveChallenge` interface, `evaluateChallenges`
  (appends to `state.challengesCompleted`, logs, fires `achievementSystem.onChallengeCompleted`)
  and `evaluateChallengesAfterAction`.
- `src/MainStreetEngineActions.ts` — calls `evaluateChallengesAfterAction` after
  every successful action, regardless of seat.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` — runs each seat's actions against the
  shared state and merges mid-turn completions into `TurnResult`.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — EndCheck safety-net evaluation.
- `src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts` — `computeScore` / `updateCompetitiveScores`
  apply one global `challengesCompleted.length * challengeBonusPoints` bonus to
  every seat.
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — `challengesCompleted: string[]`,
  `activeChallenges: ActiveChallenge[]`; per-seat `PlayerRecord` carries
  `coins`, `reputation`, `score`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` — `buildGameOverChallengeSummary`
  documents that challenges are run-global and shown once.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — renders the single challenge summary.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — shows the global challenge contribution.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetChallengeCelebration.ts` — celebration VFX keyed by
  challenge id with **no seat check**.

## Desired change

Keep **one shared challenge pool** (producer decision Q1 = B) but attribute
each completion to the seat that triggered it, and route all credit — score,
Game Over summary, celebration, HUD and achievements — through that
attribution (Q2 = A, Q3 = A). Only one player can achieve each challenge.
Single-player behaviour is unchanged.

Design outline:

1. Record the completing seat on the challenge record (e.g.
   `ActiveChallenge.completedBySeatId`), set from the acting seat at evaluation
   time (`state.activePlayerId` in competitive mode; `null`/absent for
   single-player). `evaluateChallenges` / `evaluateChallengesAfterAction`
   gain a seat context.
2. Keep `state.challengesCompleted` for single-player/back-compat; derive
   per-seat credit from the attributed records.
3. In `updateCompetitiveScores`, add `challengeBonusPoints` per seat from that
   seat's attributed completions instead of the global count.
4. `buildGameOverChallengeSummary` returns per-seat data; the overlay renders a
   per-seat breakdown.
5. Gate the celebration and the achievement bridge on the human seat in
   competitive mode.
6. Persist attribution in save/load with a legacy fallback.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetChallenges.ts` — Add completing-seat attribution to
  `evaluateChallenges` / `evaluateChallengesAfterAction`.
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — Extend `ActiveChallenge` (or add a per-seat
  completion map) to carry the completing seat.
- `src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts` — Per-seat challenge bonus in
  `updateCompetitiveScores`.
- `src/MainStreetEngineActions.ts` / `MainStreetCommands.ts` — Pass the acting
  seat into per-action evaluation.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` / `MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` —
  Carry/attribute completions through both evaluation paths.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` / `MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` —
  Per-seat challenge breakdown at game over.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetChallengeCelebration.ts` — Only celebrate the human
  seat's completions.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — Per-seat challenge contribution.
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` / `MainStreetSaveLoad.ts` — Persist
  attribution with a legacy fallback.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-play-acceptance.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/challenge-celebration-per-action.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/turnflow.test.ts` — Add per-seat attribution coverage.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUTU8J9T0034OT7** – Competitive scoreboard & active-seat HUD (completed)
- **MS-0MUXLP6V00075IQY** – Fix win/loss attribution in checkCompetitiveEndConditions for competitive mode (completed)
- **MS-0MUWDL0V40041USM** – Provide reason for game ending (completed)
- **MS-0MUNO0M2I004TK04** – Wire Main Street challenges to Steam achievements (open) — the achievement bridge is the path this bug leaks through.
- **MS-0MUVUPRXZ0030LUD** – End Turn Phase is missing in AI game (completed)
- Related docs: `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (§ Challenge,
  § Win conditions), `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` (challenge/tier
  evaluation).
- Automated find-related report is appended to the work item description.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** changing score attribution could shift competitive balance and
  break existing tests. **Mitigation:** scope the change to competitive mode
  only; single-player stays byte-for-byte compatible.
- **Risk:** save/load compatibility — new attribution fields must tolerate
  legacy saves. **Mitigation:** treat absent attribution as global/single-player.
- **Risk:** two evaluation paths (per-action and EndCheck) could double-credit.
  **Mitigation:** the `completed` flag remains the single source of truth;
  attributed seat is set once, on first completion only.
- **Assumption:** the human seat is identified via
  `controller === 'human'` / `findHumanSeatId` (existing helpers).
- **Scope-creep risk:** per-seat *challenge pools* (Q1 Option A) and new
  challenge content are out of scope; record any desire for them as a separate
  work item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Challenge ownership model in competitive mode.** Which model should
  apply?
  - (A) Each seat draws its own separate challenge set, evaluated against its
    own owner-tagged businesses.
  - (B) One shared challenge pool; each completion is attributed to the
    completing seat. **Recommended** — smallest correct change, reuses the
    owner-tagged competitive model.
  - (C) Challenges are human-only; AI actions never complete a challenge.
  - **Answer (producer): B** — one shared pool; only one player can achieve
    each challenge; each completion is credited to the completing seat.
    Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-09.

- **Q2 — Per-seat scoring.** How should a completed challenge affect scores?
  - (A) Only the credited seat receives `challengeBonusPoints`. **Recommended**
    — matches "not credited with AI challenges".
  - (B) Keep the bonus run-global for all seats and show attribution in the UI
    only.
  - (C) Remove the challenge bonus from competitive scoring entirely.
  - **Answer (producer): A** — only the credited seat receives the challenge
    bonus. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-09.

- **Q3 — UI, celebration and achievements.** How should AI completions be
  surfaced?
  - (A) Game Over shows a per-seat challenge breakdown; celebration/HUD show
    only the human seat's completions; Steam achievements unlock only for
    human completions. **Recommended** — consistent with per-seat credit.
  - (B) Single run-level summary labelled by seat; achievements unlock for
    any completion.
  - (C) Hide challenges entirely in competitive mode.
  - **Answer (producer): A** — per-seat Game Over breakdown; human-only
    celebration/HUD/achievements. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-09.

Research summary: inspected `MainStreetChallenges.ts`, `MainStreetEngineActions.ts`,
`MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts`, `MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`,
`MainStreetEngineScoring.ts`, `MainStreetStateTypes.ts`, `MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts`,
`MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`, `MainStreetChallengeCelebration.ts`, and
`docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`; confirmed challenge state is
run-global and evaluation is seat-agnostic.

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUMC6IVF0098WRL** – Add per-turn running costs to Playground, Town Fountain and Community Shelter (completed)
- **MS-0MUTU8J9T0034OT7** – Competitive scoreboard & active-seat HUD (completed)
- **MS-0MUNB58TK0025CB9** – Extend storyline options with conditional and cost-gated effects (open)

- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — matched: challenge, challenges, completions, credit, credited, including, need, player, playing, track, when, who

# Intake Brief — Identify different AI players (MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF)

> **Status: final — producer decisions incorporated (Q1=A, Q2=A, Q3=A).**
> Recorded in the Appendix below; the item advanced to `intake_complete`.

## Problem Statement

In competitive (human vs AI) Main Street games the AI seats are not visually
distinguishable from one another or, at a glance, from the human seat. The
activity log, the scoreboard and the placed-card street all identify seats only
by ad-hoc text (`P0`, `AI 1`, `AI 2`), and placed cards carry no owner
indicator at all. A player therefore cannot reliably tell which AI made a given
move or which street slots belong to which opponent. This work assigns each AI
seat a distinct, colour-blind-friendly colour and threads that colour through
the UI.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — wants to identify at a glance which AI opponent made
  a move in the log and which street cards belong to which seat.
- **Colour-blind player** — wants seat colours that remain distinguishable
  under common forms of colour-vision deficiency.
- **Future example-game authors / designers** — reuse a shared seat-colour
  palette/assignment contract rather than inventing per-game colours.

### User Stories

- As a player, when an AI takes an action I see a coloured `AI 1` / `AI 2`
  prefix in the activity log (and `You`/`Pl` for the human), so I can tell who
  acted without reading the whole line.
- As a player, every placed business/community-space card carries a border in
  its owner's colour, so I can see ownership on the street at a glance.
- As a colour-blind player, the seat colours remain mutually distinguishable
  and are never the sole carrier of meaning (the seat label text is always
  present alongside the colour).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Distinct, colour-blind-friendly seat colours (Q2 = A).** In competitive
   mode each seat (human + every AI) is assigned a distinct colour from a fixed
   colour-blind-safe palette (e.g. Okabe–Ito); the palette is shuffled per game
   with an injected RNG so the assignment is deterministic for a given seed and
   stable across save/load. Verified by unit tests on the pure assignment
   helper (palette membership, mutual distinctness, seeded determinism,
   insufficient-palette guard) and a state save/load round-trip test.
2. **Log identifies the acting seat by colour + label.** Activity-log entries
   attributable to a seat are prefixed with that seat's label (`You` for the
   human, `AI 1`, `AI 2`, …) rendered in the seat's colour, and the prefix
   remains legible against the existing gain/loss/neutral line colour. Verified
   by unit/renderer tests.
3. **Placed cards carry an owner-coloured border (Q3 = A).** Every placed
   business/community-space card on the street carries an outer border in its
   owner's colour, with human and AI seats visually distinct; the full-card
   upgrade border is removed and the upgrade indicator moves to the existing
   top-left level badge / corner accent so upgrade state stays legible.
   Verified by renderer tests plus a manual/browser check.
4. **Colour is consistent everywhere a seat is identified.** The scoreboard,
   active-seat indicator, log prefixes and card borders all derive their seat
   colour from the same lookup, so a seat has one colour throughout the UI.
   Verified by a shared palette/lookup module and tests.
5. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries** (notably
   `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` and the new module's JSDoc).
6. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Single-player is unchanged** — with one seat (the human) there are no AI
  colours and no behavioural or visual regression.
- **Colour-blind friendly** — the palette must be a recognised
  colour-vision-deficiency-safe set (e.g. Okabe–Ito) and large enough for the
  maximum supported AI opponent count; colour must never be the sole carrier of
  meaning (seat labels always accompany it).
- **Deterministic and testable** — colour assignment must accept an injected
  RNG (seeded) so it is reproducible in tests and replay, and must be persisted
  in competitive state/save so it does not reshuffle on reload.
- **Presentation-only** — no change to game rules, economy, AI decisions or
  scoring.
- **Reuse existing seams** — pure helpers must stay Phaser-free for Node unit
  tests; rendering must reuse the existing street/HUD renderers.
- **UK English spelling** in code comments, docs and UI copy.

## Existing State

- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — `PlayerRecord` has `playerId`, `controller`,
  `aiStrategy`, `aiDifficulty`, `eliminated`; **no colour field**.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCompetitiveScoreboard.ts` — labels seats `You` /
  `AI <n>`; `MainStreetRendererCompetitiveHud.ts` colours rows with hard-coded
  hex (`#aaffaa` active, `#ffcc44` human, `#88bbff` AI).
