# Create a card shader

## Problem statement

Upgraded business / community-space cards (level > 0) are currently distinguished only by a flat golden stroke, a small `Lvl N` badge, and a baked display-name variant. These read as "a normal card with a border" rather than a visibly special, premium card. The seed asks for a **custom card shader** that can be applied to upgraded cards so they look distinct at a glance on a crowded street.

**Producer decisions (2026-10-09):**
- **Q1 = A** — implement a **Canvas-compatible shader-style effect now** using the existing overlay pipeline. A true GPU shader (WebGL Filters/custom shaders) is out of scope and deferred behind a separate low-priority renderer migration (`MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK`).
- **Q2 = A** — scope is **upgraded business/community-space cards only** (level > 0).
- **Q3** — the existing **full-card golden `upgradeBorder` is being removed** by the player/AI identification work item `MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF`, which makes the owner colour the outer card border and moves the upgrade indicator to the top-left level badge / corner accent. This item must **not** depend on or recreate that full-card border; the shader effect is the upgrade distinction and must coexist with owner-coloured outer borders.
- **Q4 = as recommended** — the effect is **animated, with a reduced-motion static fallback**.
- **Q5 = default** — no regression to the existing suite; animation paused in replay/headless.

## Users

- **Main Street player (street overview)** — wants to spot upgraded businesses instantly when scanning the 2×5 street, including under competitive/owner-coloured rendering.
- **Main Street player (mid/late game)** — wants the payoff of investing in upgrades to feel visually rewarding, not just a stat change.
- **Main Street player with reduced motion enabled** — wants the same distinction in a static form.
- **Main Street developer** — wants the effect delivered through the existing upgrade overlay pipeline with a pure, testable spec builder and a Canvas-safe fallback.

Example user stories:

- As a Main Street player, I want upgraded cards to carry a distinctive animated/premium treatment so that I can tell them apart from base cards without reading the level badge.
- As a Main Street player with reduced motion enabled, I want the same distinction in a static form so that the game stays comfortable to use.
- As a Main Street developer, I want the effect driven by a pure spec builder so that it can be unit-tested without a Phaser runtime.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Upgraded business/community-space cards (level > 0) render a distinctive shader-style effect** (e.g. animated gradient/shimmer on the corner accent / inner glow) via the existing overlay pipeline, with **no change to the Phaser render type**; base cards (level 0) render unchanged.
2. The effect is driven by a **pure, Phaser-free spec** (extending `buildUpgradeOverlaySpec` or a sibling pure module) so it is unit-testable, and the spec builder's base-card output is unchanged (`null` effect for level 0).
3. **Reduced-motion behaviour is respected:** when `settingsPanel.reducedMotion` is true the effect degrades to a static (non-animated) form; no animation runs in replay/headless mode.
4. **The effect does not depend on, recreate, or conflict with the full-card upgrade border.** It must coexist with the owner-coloured outer border introduced by `MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF` (owner colour remains the outer border; the shader effect is confined to the upgrade accent), and colour must never be the sole carrier of meaning.
5. **Test/validation criterion:** new unit tests cover the spec builder for base vs upgraded cards (and reduced-motion), plus a browser integration test asserting the effect is attached to an upgraded card and absent on a base card.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (in particular `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` § "Card Upgrade Rendering Pipeline" and `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md`).
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No renderer change (fixed):** the game boots with `type: Phaser.CANVAS` (`main.ts`); the effect must work under Canvas. Phaser custom shaders / `postFX` pipelines are WebGL-only and are explicitly **out of scope** for this item.
- **Scope:** only upgraded (level > 0) business / community-space cards. Upgrade-family card faces, events, staff and base cards are out of scope.
- **Coordination with `MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF`:** that item removes `spec.upgradeBorder` and makes the owner colour the outer card border; this item's effect must sit inside/alongside that (upgrade accent / level badge), never as a full-card stroke.
- Upgraded-card textures are cached once per base card (one texture key per base card, plus a display-name variant); the effect must not multiply texture-cache keys per level.
- Presentation-only: the effect must never mutate game state, transcript, or replay output, and must be skipped in replay/headless mode.
- Reuse the existing overlay pipeline (`src/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` + `MainStreetRenderer.applyUpgradeOverlays()`); do not re-rasterise the card SVG on every state change.
- Accessibility: must honour the existing reduced-motion setting (`settingsPanel.reducedMotion`).
- Keep the existing level badge and stat overlays readable and un-occluded; the 64×64 left-art zone and right-hand text column layout (`CG-0MTORJ5FS006B0UN`) must be preserved.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` — pure spec builder for upgraded cards: `levelBadge`, `cashLine`, `reputationText`, `upgradeBorder` (flat golden `0xffaa22`, 3 px). This is the natural extension point; note `upgradeBorder` is slated for removal by `MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — `applyUpgradeOverlays()` creates the Phaser rectangle/text objects from the spec.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — SVG card faces; upgraded name baked into a display-name variant texture (`CG-0MT24MHGZ0025O20`).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetSvgTextureManager.ts` — rasterises SVG → texture (one key per base card; DPR-aware).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimator*` — existing upgrade level-up burst (`animateLevelUp`) and reduced-motion handling; precedent for presentation-only, replay-safe effects.
- `core/example-games/gym/scenes/GymGraphicsShaderSpikeScene.ts` — an isolated spike that evaluates sprite tinting and blend modes (NORMAL/ADD/MULTIPLY/SCREEN). It documents shader *feasibility* but does **not** implement a custom fragment shader; it runs under `Phaser.CANVAS`.
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` § "Card Upgrade Rendering Pipeline" documents the current overlay architecture and explicitly rejects per-level SVG variants.
- `main.ts` / `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — both pin `type: Phaser.CANVAS`.
- `MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF` — seat colours / owner-coloured card borders; removes the full-card upgrade border.

## Desired change

Extend `UpgradeOverlaySpec` with a shader-style effect spec (e.g. animated gradient/shimmer accent) and render it with Phaser `Graphics` + tweens in `applyUpgradeOverlays()`. No renderer change; works under Canvas; reduced-motion → static gradient. Base cards unchanged; presentation-only; the pure spec builder remains unit-testable. The effect replaces the *upgrade indicator role* of the removed full-card border without reintroducing a full-card stroke, and coexists with owner-coloured outer borders.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` — add the effect spec (colour stops, animation params, reduced-motion static form); reconcile with `upgradeBorder` removal.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — render the effect in `applyUpgradeOverlays()`; add cleanup/tween lifecycle; reconcile with owner-coloured border.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererContext.ts` — extend the renderer interface if the effect needs a new method.
- `tests/main-street/UpgradeOverlaySpec.test.ts` — unit tests for the effect spec (base vs upgraded, reduced-motion).
- `tests/main-street/*.browser.test.ts` — browser integration test asserting the effect is present on an upgraded card and absent on a base card.
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — update the "Card Upgrade Rendering Pipeline" section.
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — document the effect, triggers, and reduced-motion behaviour.

## Related work

Manually identified:

- `MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF` — Identify different AI players (open, intake_complete) — **owns the owner-coloured outer card border and removes the full-card upgrade border**; this item's effect must integrate with it. Both touch `UpgradeOverlaySpec` / `applyUpgradeOverlays`, so sequence or coordinate to avoid rework.
- `MS-0MUZH51PU007POJ4` — Colour card faces by synergy type (two-tone bridge cards) (open) — adjacent card-face visual change; coordinate so the shader and synergy colouring do not clash.
- `MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E` — Assign dedicated card art to every Main Street card (open) — owns the card-art/texture pipeline this effect must coexist with.
- `MS-0MUDYQQ2E00913QN` — Synergy tooltip (completed) — prior card visual/overlay work.
- `MS-0MUGRKEWZ0073327` — Move level label to left (completed) — prior upgraded-card overlay adjustment.

## Deferred work

- **`MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK`** — Migrate Main Street renderer from Canvas to WebGL (deferred; prerequisite for GPU shaders) (open, low priority) — created as a separate `discovered-from` item. A true GPU card shader depends on it. **Not a blocker** for this item.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Renderer risk (resolved):** Option A keeps the Canvas renderer, so no renderer/CI change is required.
- **Coordination risk (`MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF`):** both items modify `UpgradeOverlaySpec` / `applyUpgradeOverlays`; if implemented out of order the upgrade border may be added then removed. Mitigation: agree sequencing (owner-border item first is cleanest) and keep this effect to the upgrade accent, not a full-card stroke.
- **Performance risk:** an always-animating effect on every upgraded card could regress frame rate and headless CI. Mitigation: cap animated cards, pause when off-screen/replay, and provide a static form.
- **Accessibility risk:** animation without a reduced-motion fallback. Mitigation: AC3.
- **Testability risk:** Phaser rendering is hard to unit-test. Mitigation: keep the effect as a pure spec (AC2) and assert spec + presence in a browser test (AC5).
- **Visual-conflict risk:** clashes with owner-coloured competitive rendering (`MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF`) and future synergy colouring (`MS-0MUZH51PU007POJ4`). Mitigation: keep the effect to the border/accent layer, never the sole carrier of meaning, and avoid the outer border band.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "card shader" could expand to all card families, animated backgrounds, foil effects, etc. Mitigation: scope to upgraded (level > 0) business/community-space cards; record extra opportunities as linked work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (approach):** What does "card shader" mean for this project, given the game runs under `Phaser.CANVAS` (custom GPU shaders are WebGL-only)? Options: **(A)** a Canvas-compatible shader-style effect using the existing overlay pipeline; **(B)** switch to WebGL and implement a true custom fragment shader; **(C)** bake an SVG filter/gradient into the upgraded card texture. — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-09): Option A** — Canvas-compatible effect now, with a **deferred, low-priority migration to WebGL**. Source: interactive reply. Research: `main.ts` pins `Phaser.CANVAS`; Phaser 4.0.0-rc.7 has no WebGPU backend; `GeometryMask` is Canvas-only and used across Main Street + core UI, so the WebGL migration is a substantial separate effort (`MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK`).
- **Q2 (scope):** Which cards should receive the effect? Options: (a) upgraded business/community-space cards only (level > 0); (b) also upgrade-family card faces; (c) all cards. — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-09): (a)** — upgraded business/community-space cards only.
- **Q3 (existing border):** Replace the flat golden `upgradeBorder`, complement it, or restyle it? — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-09):** the full-card border is **being removed by the player/AI identification work** (`MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF`), which makes the owner colour the outer card border and moves the upgrade indicator to the level badge / corner accent. This item therefore adds the upgrade shader accent and must not depend on/recreate the full-card border.
- **Q4 (motion):** Static or animated? — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-09): as recommended** — animated, with a reduced-motion static fallback (AC3).
- **Q5 (performance):** Explicit performance/device budget? — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-09): default accepted** — no regression to the existing suite; animation paused in replay/headless.

**Research finding (agent, 2026-10-09):** The current upgrade distinction is a flat golden border + `Lvl N` badge + baked display name, built by the pure `UpgradeOverlaySpec` and rendered by `applyUpgradeOverlays()` (`src/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts`). The game boots with `type: Phaser.CANVAS` (`main.ts`, `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`), and the engine documents Canvas as a deliberate CI-performance choice (`core/src/ui/createCardGame.ts`). The gym "Shader & Blend Spike" only exercises tint/blend modes — it does not implement a custom fragment shader. Therefore Option A (Canvas-compatible effect) is the feasible path now, with a true GPU shader deferred behind the WebGL migration (`MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK`). `MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF` will remove the full-card upgrade border, so the upgrade distinction must move to the level badge / corner accent this effect targets.

# Perform end of turn phase for each player (MS-0MUXAQQON006XA6I)

## Problem statement

In competitive (human vs AI) mode the shared closing (Income → Incident → EndCheck) is presented as a single condensed, text-only summary. The full end-of-turn income choreography that single-player players see — base → synergy → reputation → events → upcoming → grid-to-HUD coin collection, with per-card coin grids and sound — never runs for the AI seats (nor for the human seat). Much of the end-of-turn phase is therefore lost in an AI game.

## Users

- **Competitive mode players** (especially the human seat) who want to see the outcome of each player's day — what each seat earned and what effects fired — with the same visual feedback as single-player, rather than an unexplained jump to the next day.
- **Maintainers** who want a single end-of-turn presentation path so the single-player and competitive flows cannot drift.

Example user stories:
- "As a competitive player, after I end my day I want to watch each player's income collection in turn, so I understand how the shared day changed every seat's economy."
- "As a competitive player on a slow machine, I want the AI closing to be short and skippable, so playing against AI does not take many minutes per day."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1: Per-seat full closing presentation** — After the shared competitive closing resolves, the presentation runs the full phased income choreography (`animateIncomePhases`: base → synergy → reputation → events → upcoming → grid-to-HUD collection) once per non-eliminated seat, in seat order, using that seat's own income/effects. The human seat is included; eliminated seats are skipped.
- **AC2: Authoritative per-seat data** — The competitive closing surfaces the per-owner income (`applyCompetitiveIncome` → `OwnerIncomeResult[]`, which already carries a full `IncomeResult.phaseBreakdown`) instead of discarding it, and every presented per-seat value equals the delta actually applied to that `PlayerRecord` (asserted by test).
- **AC3: Per-seat income feedback text** — The closing summary reports each seat's income (e.g. `Player 2: +7 coins`), not the shared host total, which can differ from any player's actual income.
- **AC4: Shared engine semantics unchanged** — Presentation-only change: the closing order (Income → Incident → EndCheck), the single shared incident per day, and seeded-replay determinism are unchanged.
- **AC5: Single presentation primitive** — Single-player and competitive closings are driven by one shared presentation path; `finishTurnPresentation` and `presentCompetitiveClosing` no longer duplicate the income/incident/end-of-turn/advance logic. Single-player behaviour is behaviourally unchanged (existing turn-flow tests pass without modification). This absorbs **MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ**.
- **AC6: Bounded and non-blocking** — Full animations run in normal play; reduced motion, replay and headless contexts fall back to per-seat text and always advance the day; a global fast-forward bound caps total closing time so a large roster cannot stall the game (honours MS-0MUVUPRXZ0030LUD AC4).
- **AC7: Tests** — New/updated automated tests cover: per-seat animation sequencing (one full choreography per non-eliminated seat, in order), authoritative per-seat values (presented == applied deltas), bounded/headless fallback (day always advances; text-only when animations are disabled), and single-player unchanged.
- **AC8: Documentation** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC9: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Presentation-only** (producer decision Q2-A): no change to the engine closing order or the shared-incident contract; income/incident still resolve once per shared day.
- **Bounded** (producer decision Q3-A): the closing must never block the day start indefinitely; reduced motion / replay / headless degrade to text.
- **Determinism**: the presentation must not consume RNG or mutate state (beyond reusing the existing deferred-delta window where applicable), so seeded replay stays reproducible.
- **Single-player parity**: single-player end-of-turn presentation and its deferred-mutation flow (CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q) must not regress.
- Phaser-free helpers where possible, so the node integration tests can exercise the flow (`MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive` is already Phaser-free).

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts`
  - `endCompetitiveTurnDay` → `driveAiSeatsUntilClosing` → `runCompetitiveClosing` → `presentCompetitiveClosing` → `startTurnPhase`.
  - `presentCompetitiveClosing` shows `Resolving end-of-turn effects...`, a one-line `competitiveClosingSummary` built from the **shared** `result.income.total` and the incident name, then `End of turn complete.` after a ~900 ms hold. It deliberately does **not** run `animateIncomePhases` (test `competitive-closing-presentation.test.ts` asserts `incomeCalls` is empty).
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` — `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases` calls `applyCompetitiveIncome(state)` and **discards** the returned `OwnerIncomeResult[]`; `TurnResult.income` carries only the shared `applyIncome` result. `applyCompetitiveIncome` already builds a per-owner `IncomeResult` with a full `SlotPhaseBreakdown[]`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — single-player `endTurn` delegates to `processEndOfTurn` (with `deferResourceApplication`) then `animateIncomePhases`, then `finishTurnPresentation`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncome.ts` — `animateIncomePhases(animator, phaseData, options)` runs the phased choreography from `SlotPhaseBreakdown[]` (indexed against the shared street grid) and applies `options.pendingDeltas` exactly once at collection completion; `incomeCollectionActive` gates the HUD delta pop.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererCompetitiveHud.ts` — the competitive HUD binds each row to that seat's `state.players` coins/reputation/score (so a per-seat collection can land on the right row).

# Piggyback on other players' organiser actions

## Problem statement

In competitive (human vs AI) play, when one player organises a town-wide event such as a Local Festival, the benefits are currently routed only to that acting player's own wallet (`applyCompetitiveEventEffects`). There is no way for the other player(s) to participate in, or benefit from, an event that thematically belongs to the whole town. This makes events feel private rather than communal and removes a legible, interesting per-event decision from the non-acting player.

## Users

Primary user: the **human player in competitive mode**, who wants a meaningful reactive decision when the AI organises a town event.

- As the human player, when the AI organises a festival, I want to choose whether to co-fund it so that I can earn the full reward, or simply enjoy the spill-over benefit for free.
- As the human player, I want the trade-off to be explicit (coins and action cost vs. reward share) so the decision is legible.
- Secondary user: the **AI seat**, which needs a deterministic policy for the same decision so headless Monte Carlo runs stay reproducible.

## Proposed mechanic (design summary)

When a player plays a **piggyback-eligible Investment event** (an "organiser" event — e.g. Local Festival, Harvest Festival) during their MarketPhase, every **other active player** receives a 50% share of that event's rewards **automatically**, and is offered the single choice to **join fully**:

| Option | Cost | Reward |
|--------|------|--------|
| **Join fully** | **150% of the cost the acting player paid for the event** (paid from the piggybacker's own coins); **no action point is spent** | **100%** of the event's rewards |
| **Free-ride (automatic default)** | Nothing | **50%** of the event's rewards, granted automatically |

- The free-ride 50% is always applied, so there is **no "decline everything" option** and no prompt to refuse it — the only decision is whether to pay to upgrade 50% → 100%.
- Joining fully does **not** consume an action point; the seed's "take an additional action" means the player participates in the event (an additional participant), not that a budget action is spent.
- Rewards (coin + reputation) are computed on the **piggybacker's own board**, consistent with the existing per-owner event routing (`SpecificSynergy` rewards count the owner's own matching businesses), then scaled to 100% (join fully) or 50% (free-ride).
- The cost baseline is the amount the acting player **actually paid** for the event (after any cost discounts the acting player holds), not necessarily the card's nominal listed cost.
- If the piggybacker cannot afford 150% of that cost, the join-fully option is unavailable and the 50% free-ride applies.
- The acting player's own reward, and the shared market/incident deck, are unaffected by piggyback decisions.
- The mechanic applies **only in competitive mode (N≥2)**; single-player (N=1) has no other players and is unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Eligibility & trigger.** When an active player plays a piggyback-eligible **organiser** Investment event during their MarketPhase in competitive mode (N≥2), every other non-eliminated player automatically receives the 50% free-ride share and is offered the join-fully upgrade for that event; playing a non-eligible event (or any event in N=1) produces no share and no prompt. Verified by unit tests over a flagged eligible card and an unflagged card.
- [ ] **AC2 — Join-fully tier.** Choosing "join fully" deducts exactly 150% of the cost the acting player paid for the event from the piggybacker's own coin balance (and **no action point**), then credits the piggybacker 100% of the event's rewards (computed on their own board). The option is unavailable (and never partially charged) when the piggybacker cannot afford the cost. Verified by unit tests asserting exact before/after coin and reputation values and an unchanged action budget.
- [ ] **AC3 — Free-ride tier.** Every non-acting eligible player automatically receives 50% of the event's rewards (computed on their own board) with no prompt to decline, spending no action point and no coins. This is also the fallback when "join fully" is unaffordable. Verified by unit tests.
- [ ] **AC4 — Isolation, determinism & persistence.** The acting player's reward and all shared decks are byte-for-byte unchanged by piggyback decisions; decisions for N>2 are resolved independently per seat in a deterministic order with no additional RNG draws; a pending piggyback decision survives a save/load round-trip. Verified by tests (including a replay/equality check and a serialize→deserialize→resolve test).
- [ ] **AC5 — AI policy and human prompt.** AI seats decide whether to join fully via a deterministic strategy heuristic in `MainStreetAiStrategy`; the human seat is offered the choice to join fully (pay the cost for 100%) or keep the automatic 50% free-ride, through the existing choice/prompt plumbing. Verified by an AI-policy unit test and a scene/command-layer test for the human prompt.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `docs/main-street/ai-strategy.md`, and any relevant PRD/scope notes.
- [ ] **AC7 — Tests.** New unit tests cover eligibility, both tiers, the unaffordable fallback, N>2 isolation, AI policy and save/load; the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Presentation and economy scale.** Costs in this game are large (Local Festival lists at 300 coins; Harvest Festival and similar events are comparable). 150% of a 300-coin event is 450 — a significant sink — so the AI heuristic and the human prompt must state the exact coin cost and the resulting reward share.
- **Determinism.** Competitive mode is exercised by a headless Monte Carlo harness and deterministic replay/transcript tests; the mechanic must not introduce additional RNG draws in the resolution path.
- **Per-owner authority.** `PlayerRecord.coins` / `.reputation` are authoritative in competitive mode (the shared `resourceBank` is a scratch mirror). Piggyback cost and reward must mutate the piggybacker's `PlayerRecord`, not the shared wallet.
- **Backwards compatibility.** Adding a per-card eligibility flag must default to "not eligible" so existing card data and save files are unaffected; older saves without the pending-piggyback field must load with a null default.
- **Turn terminology.** Use canonical "turn"/"week" vocabulary; player-facing text is guarded by `scripts/check-terminology-guards.sh`.

## Existing state

- Competitive mode (N players on one owner-tagged street, alternating MarketPhases within a shared day) is implemented engine-side. `MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` orchestrates the shared day; `endCompetitiveMarketTurn` round-robins seats.
- Investment events are played during the acting seat's MarketPhase via `playEventFromHand` (`MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts`) and dispatchers in `MainStreetEngineActions.ts` (`buy-event`, `play-event`, `play-event-from-hand`).
- `applyCompetitiveEventEffects` (`MainStreetEngineEvents.ts`) already routes an Investment event's deltas to the **acting player only** (`actingId`), and computes `SpecificSynergy` rewards per owner from that owner's matching businesses. This is the natural seam for a scaled (100%/50%) piggyback reward.
- Per-card data lives in `src/card-data.csv` with an extensive column set; event rows currently carry `trigger`, `effect`, `target`, `targetSynergy`, `coinDelta`, `reputationDelta`, `hasChoices`, `acceptNextCardId`, `rejectNextCardId`, etc. There is **no** piggyback/eligibility column yet.
- A precedent for deferring a player decision already exists: dual-choice incidents stash `state.pendingEventChoice` and pause the turn with `TurnResult.choicePending`, then resolve via `resolveEventChoice` / `resolveEventOption`; the pending choice is serialized in `MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`. The piggyback decision should reuse this "pending decision + pause/resume" pattern.
- AI action enumeration and scoring live in `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`; there is no piggyback decision yet, and no repo occurrence of "piggyback" anywhere.
- Actions are budgeted per seat (`PlayerRecord.actionBudget`) and partly bankable (`state.bankedActions`, capped at 2). Piggybacking does **not** spend an action point; the acting player's normal action consumption is unchanged.

## Desired change

- Add a per-card **piggyback-eligibility** flag (CSV column + `EventCard` field) defaulting to false, and mark organiser events such as Local Festival / Harvest Festival as eligible.
- When an eligible event is played in competitive mode, raise a **pending piggyback decision** for each other active player; pause/resume the shared day using the existing pending-choice pattern so the acting player's resolution completes first.
- Apply the chosen tier: join fully = −150% of the cost the acting player paid, +100% rewards (no action cost); free-ride = +50% rewards, applied automatically. Rewards are computed from the piggybacker's own board via the existing per-owner event math (then scaled).
- Add a deterministic **AI join-fully policy** and a **human prompt** offering join-fully vs. keep-50% (no decline option).
- Serialize/deserialize the pending decision; keep older saves loading.
- Update docs, code comments and tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — new `piggybackable` column; mark organiser event rows (Local Festival, Harvest Festival, …) as eligible.
- `src/MainStreetCards.ts` / `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — parse and expose the eligibility flag on `EventCard`.
- `src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts` — `playEventFromHand` / `playHeldEvent` hook that raises piggyback opportunities after the acting player's event resolves.
- `src/MainStreetEngineEvents.ts` — reward computation seam: scale and route event rewards to a piggybacker's own wallet.
- `src/MainStreetEngineActions.ts` — cover both event-play dispatch paths (`play-event`, `play-event-from-hand`); new piggyback `PlayerAction` variants if needed.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` / `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — pending-piggyback state machine, pause/resume of the shared day.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts` / `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — pending-piggyback state shape and action/result types.
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` / `src/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts` — persist the pending decision with a null default for older saves.
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — deterministic AI piggyback decision policy.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts` (+ overlay/HUD renderers) — human prompt for the decision.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `docs/main-street/ai-strategy.md` — document the mechanic, tiers and AI policy.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption — competitive-only scope.** The mechanic applies only when N≥2; single-player has no other player to piggyback on. Revisit only if a solo "friendly town" flavour is later wanted.
- **Confirmed — free-ride is automatic.** Per the producer, the 50% free-ride is always applied and never offered as a decline option; the only player decision is whether to pay to upgrade to 100%.
- **Confirmed — no action-point cost.** Joining fully spends coins only (150% of the acting player's paid cost); the action budget is untouched.
- **Risk — economy runaway.** Stacking 100%-reward participation across many organiser events could inflate a seat's economy. Mitigation: the 150% cost premium; re-run the competitive Monte Carlo harness and record before/after win-rate/score attribution.
- **Risk — turn-resume complexity.** Pausing the shared day to await a piggyback decision touches the same deferred-closing machinery as dual-choice incidents. Mitigation: reuse the `pendingEventChoice` pattern and cover pause/resume + save/load with dedicated tests (AC4/AC5).
- **Risk — AI legality.** The AI must never attempt the full tier without the action or coins. Mitigation: share one affordability predicate between the eligibility gate and the AI policy, tested directly.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Extending piggybacking to business purchases/upgrades/staff hires is out of scope unless Q1 selects option (c); record any such desire as a separate linked work item rather than expanding this one.

## Related work

- `MS-0MTIIL6J200291ZQ` — *Per-owner income routing; shared event/incident resolution* (feature, completed) — establishes the per-owner event routing this mechanic builds on.
- `MS-0MT5X3GMA007EG30` — *Main Street competitive mode: AI opponent on the shared street* (epic, done) — the competitive engine this mechanic extends.
- `MS-0MTSHG8RP008E128` — dual-choice incident deferred-resolution pattern (referenced in code comments; the save/load and pause/resume precedent to reuse).
- `MS-0MUVUPWHD0032CU4` — *Turns do not bank when playing against AI* (completed) — action-budget/banking rules a piggyback action must respect.
- `MS-0MUVQRBVI0015AB2` — *AI seat elimination with business closure* (completed) — defines "other active players" (non-eliminated seats only).
- `MS-0MUR9IN7L0004TO5` — *Re-price community spaces and events…* (completed) — the event cost/reward baseline used by the 150%/100%/50% maths.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

The seed intent was clear on the headline rule but left several design details open. All questions below were answered by the producer on 2026-10-07; the confirmed answers are recorded inline and the brief has been updated to match.

- **Q1 — Which actions are piggyback-eligible?** — Answer (producer): **organiser events only** (option a) — a per-card opt-in flag on Investment "organiser" events (festivals, fairs, community gatherings); not all Investment events and not purchases/upgrades/staff hires. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.
- **Q2 — What does "take an additional action" mean, and is the 50% tier a choice?** — Answer (producer): joining fully **does not cost an action point**; it costs **150% of the cost paid by the original (acting) player**. There is no point in declining the 50% free-ride, so **no decline option is offered** — the 50% share is automatic and the only decision is whether to pay to upgrade to 100%. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.
- **Q3 — Reward and cost baseline for the piggybacker.** — Answer (producer): **confirm** — rewards are the event's deltas computed on the **piggybacker's own board** (per-owner `SpecificSynergy` matching), scaled ×1.0 (join fully) / ×0.5 (free-ride); the cost is 150% of the cost the acting player paid (per Q2). Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.
- **Q4 — Multi-player prompt ordering and simultaneous decisions.** — Answer (producer): **as recommended** — decisions are solicited and resolved one seat at a time in seat order, independently per seat, before the shared day continues. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.

# Intake Brief: Generate Mermaid diagrams for card synergies, staff relationships and upgrade chains (MS-0MUYK5BEC007L61X)

**Priority: Low** | **Type: Feature** | **Assignee: Map**
**Producer decisions (2026-10-07, interactive): Q1 = A (docs/tooling artefacts); Q2 = B (named three + community-space extension); Q3 = A (committed `.mmd` + `--check` drift guard).** See Appendix.

## Problem statement

The repo already generates a deterministic Mermaid flowchart of the storyline
graph (`src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` → `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd`,
with a JSON manifest and a `--check` drift guard), but no other card dataset is
visualised. Designers, reviewers and new contributors must reconstruct card
synergies, staff coverage, upgrade chains and community-space relationships by
reading 174 CSV rows. Generating the same class of deterministic Mermaid
diagram for these datasets makes each relationship legible at a glance and
keeps the pictures drift-guarded against `src/card-data.csv`.

## Users

- **Content designer / producer** — sees at a glance which cards share a synergy,
  which staff can serve which businesses, and how upgrade chains branch and gate.
  - *"As a designer, I want a Mermaid diagram of card synergies, so I can check
    that every synergy type has a healthy cluster of cards without reading the CSV."*
  - *"As a designer, I want a diagram of staff coverage, so I can spot uncovered
    business types or overly broad staff."*
  - *"As a designer, I want a diagram of upgrade chains, so I can see the two-step
    level-1 → level-2 branches and their gates."*
- **Reviewer / balancer** — trusts the committed diagrams because a drift guard
  fails when they fall out of sync with `src/card-data.csv`.
- **New contributor / developer** — uses the diagrams as an entry point to the
  card model, alongside `card-catalog.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Diagram generator CLI.** A new dev-only npm script (e.g. `npm run
   docs:diagrams`) generates Mermaid from `src/card-data.csv` through the typed
   card model under `vite-node`, supporting `--diagram
   <synergies|staff|upgrades|community-spaces|all>` (default `all`), `--format
   mermaid|json` (default `mermaid`), `--out <path>` and `--check` (drift guard:
   exit `1` on drift, `0` when up to date). Verified by unit tests that invoke
   the CLI and assert its exit codes and output.
2. **Committed artefacts & drift guard.** Four deterministic Mermaid artefacts
   are committed under `docs/main-street/` — `card-synergies.mmd`,
   `staff-relationships.mmd`, `upgrade-chains.mmd`,
   `community-space-relationships.mmd` — and a Vitest drift guard regenerates
   each from `src/card-data.csv` and fails when the committed file differs
   byte-for-byte. The existing `storyline-graph.mmd` drift guard continues to pass.
3. **Card synergy diagram content.** Shows every business and community-space
   card and all six synergy types (Food, Culture, Service, Commerce,
   Entertainment, Health), with an edge per card↔synergy membership so cards that
   can chain adjacency bonuses are identifiable. Verified by unit tests asserting
   the exact node set plus edges for representative multi-synergy cards (e.g.
   `biz-cafe` → Food + Culture; `cs-public-art` → Culture + Entertainment) and
   that all six synergy types appear.

# Colour card faces by synergy type (two-tone bridge cards)

## Problem statement

Business and community-space cards are currently rendered with a neutral dark-grey
face (`#2f2f2f`); only a faint synergy-accent header bar, the 64×64 art backing and
the synergy icons carry the synergy colour. Players therefore cannot read a card's
synergy type — or, for a bridge card, both of its synergy types — directly from the
card face, which weakens at-a-glance planning when the market row mixes single- and
multi-synergy cards. The card face should be coloured by synergy type, and bridge
cards (exactly two synergy types) should show both colours, split top and bottom.

## Users

- **Main Street player (build planner)** — scanning the market row and their street,
  wants to identify a card's synergy type(s) instantly without reading the icon row or
  opening a tooltip.

Example user stories:

- As a Main Street player scanning the market, I want each business/community-space
  card coloured by its synergy type, so that I can tell Food from Culture at a glance.
- As a Main Street player evaluating a bridge card, I want to see both of its synergy
  colours (top and bottom), so that I immediately understand it connects two clusters.
- As a player with colour-vision deficiency, I still want an unambiguous cue (the
  synergy icons), so that colour is not the only signal.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Single-synergy face colour.** Every business and community-space card with
  exactly one synergy type renders its card face in that synergy type's face colour
  from a single shared, documented palette, replacing the current neutral `#2f2f2f`
  face. The mapping is the single source of truth used by every generator.
- **AC2 — Two-tone bridge face.** Every card with exactly two synergy types renders
  its face split horizontally into two colour bands — **top band = first entry in
  `synergyTypes`, bottom band = second entry** — using the same palette. The rounded
  card corners and the existing inner gradient / header-bar treatments are preserved,
  and neither band bleeds outside the rounded rectangle.
- **AC3 — Both synergies identifiable; colour is not the only cue.** Each bridge card
  continues to render **both** synergy icons (bottom-left), and the title/stat text
  remains white and legible on both bands; cards remain identifiable under hand
  overlap (~20 px) and street stacking (~23 px) (existing layout contract
  CG-0MTORJ5FS006B0UN). Cards with zero synergy types (event / upgrade / staff) keep
  their existing family colours unchanged.
- **AC4 — All render paths agree.** The static Node generator
  (`generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`), the runtime CSV fallback
  (`generateCardSvgFromCsvRow`) and the dynamic state-aware generator
  (`generateBusinessCardSvg`) all produce the same synergy colouring/split, and the
  pre-baked SVGs in `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/` plus
  `csv-checksum.json` are regenerated.
- **AC5 — Tests.** Unit tests cover: single-synergy cards use the matching palette
  colour; bridge cards emit two bands with the correct top/bottom palette colours and
  band geometry; zero-synergy cards are unchanged; the TS and mjs generators agree;
  and the shipped static SVGs reflect the colouring (regression guard). Existing SVG
  tests (`card-svg-generator.test.ts`, `mjs-svg-generator.test.ts`, `card-art.test.ts`,
  currency/ongoing-cost tests) continue to pass.
- **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, `README.md` where relevant, and the Main Street docs
  (`docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` bridge section and any card-rendering/design
  notes).
- **AC7 — Quality gate.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Rendering-only:** no engine, rules, scoring, adjacency, balance, or card-data (CSV)
  changes. `synergyTypes` is already the source of truth.
- **One palette:** a single documented synergy→face-colour map is the source of truth.
  The `.mjs` static generator cannot import the TS module, so the values are duplicated
  in the two places with a test asserting agreement — following the existing pattern
  used for staff cost text.
- **Two types maximum today** (CSV distribution: 29 single-synergy, 10 bridge,
  135 none). Behaviour for >2 synergy types is out of scope; the implementation must
  degrade safely (e.g. fall back to a single/first colour) rather than throw.
- **Preserve the existing card layout:** 64×64 left-art zone, text positions, cost
  badge, level badge, synergy icons and embedded art (CG-0MTORJ5FS006B0UN).
- **UK English** in code comments and documentation.

## Existing state

- Runtime cards are rasterised from static SVGs generated by
  `src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` (`generateCardSvg`) and refreshed
  from the CSV at runtime by `generateCardSvgFromCsvRow`
  (`src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts`), driven by `MainStreetSvgTextureManager`.
- `familyColor()` (mjs) and `cardColorScheme()` (TS) give business and community-space
  cards a neutral face (`#2f2f2f`); synergy colour is applied only to the graphic
  backing (`opacity 0.42`), the 20 px header bar (`opacity 0.18`) and the synergy icons.
- `synergyColor` (bright palette) is used for icons/accents; `CARD_BG` (dark palette)
  exists in the TS generator for `generateBusinessCardSvg` and is currently the only
  place a synergy-coloured face is used.
- 39 business/community-space cards: 29 single-synergy, 10 bridge — Cafe, Food Truck,
  Art Gallery, Day Spa, Flower Shop, Juice Bar, Yoga Studio, Physiotherapist,
  Teahouse, Public Art.
- `generateBusinessCardSvg` (dynamic) is used only by tests today; the runtime texture
  path is the CSV/static pair — but it must stay consistent.

## Desired change

- Introduce a documented synergy→face-colour palette (reuse `CARD_BG`) and a helper
  that computes the face background: one colour for single-synergy cards, a top/bottom
  colour pair for bridge cards.
- Update the `.mjs` and TS generators to paint the face with that helper, splitting
  bridge faces horizontally (top = `synergyTypes[0]`, bottom = `synergyTypes[1]`)
  inside the rounded rect (clip path or two rounded/clipped rects).
- Regenerate the static SVGs and `csv-checksum.json`.
- Add/update tests and documentation.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` — face background via palette +
  top/bottom split for bridge cards; expose the mapping for tests.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — `cardColorScheme` /
  `generateCardSvgFromCsvRow` and `generateBusinessCardSvg` face colouring + split;
  shared `CARD_BG` palette.
- `src/MainStreetCardsUtils.ts` — canonical `synergyColor` (bright palette) reference;
  add the dark face palette here if it should be shared.
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/*.svg` — regenerated, especially
  `biz-cafe.svg`, `biz-food-truck.svg`, `biz-gallery.svg`, `biz-spa.svg`,
  `biz-florist.svg`, `biz-juice-bar.svg`, `biz-yoga-studio.svg`, `biz-physio.svg`,
  `biz-teahouse.svg`, `cs-public-art.svg`.
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/csv-checksum.json` — regenerated checksum.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetSvgTextureManager.ts` — read-only; verify the runtime CSV
  fallback picks up the colouring (no change expected).
- `tests/main-street/card-svg-generator.test.ts` — face-colour + bridge split
  assertions.
- `tests/main-street/mjs-svg-generator.test.ts` — static-SVG regression guard for the
  split + TS/mjs agreement.
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — verify no regression in art embedding with the
  new backgrounds.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — document the colour scheme / bridge two-tone rule.

## Related work

- `MS-0MUDYQQ2E00913QN` (completed) — Synergy tooltip.
- `MS-0MTSAWSME004BH6S` (completed) — Add images for all cards.
- `MS-0MTIILOLR002ZU9K` (completed) — Competitive rendering: owner-coloured street,
  shared-market phase alternation, SFX.
- `MS-0MUGRKEWZ0073327` (completed) — Move level label to left (same SVG layout code).
- `MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E` (open) — Assign dedicated card art to every Main Street card
  (touches the art backing in the same generator).
- `MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF` (open) — Identify different AI players (shared
  colour-blind-friendliness concern).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (palette):** use the existing dark `CARD_BG` palette for the card face
  (readable with white text), keeping the bright `synergyColor` palette for
  icons/accents. The producer may prefer the bright palette — a small, localised switch.
- **Assumption (split):** horizontal split, top band = first entry in the CSV
  `synergyTypes` order, bottom = second, matching the operator's "top and bottom".
- **Assumption (scope):** applies to business + community-space cards in all three
  generators; event/upgrade/staff keep family colours; no >2-synergy cards exist today.
- **Risk (generator drift):** the mjs and TS generators hold separate copies of the
  colour logic. Mitigation: shared constant values plus an agreement test.
- **Risk (contrast/readability):** full colour faces may reduce text contrast,
  especially under the 0.18 header overlay. Mitigation: dark palette, keep the synergy
  icons as a secondary cue, and visually check in the browser test.
- **Risk (stale static assets):** forgetting to regenerate the static SVGs / checksum
  leaves the game showing old faces. Mitigation: regenerate in the same change and add
  a shipped-SVG regression test.
- **Risk (scope creep):** card-art redesign, per-owner tile tints, or synergy-icon
  additions are out of scope — record as linked work items, do not implement here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive round was run — the operator's seed directive plus repo research
sufficed to draft a clear brief. The design defaults below are recorded as **assumed
(recommended option)**; the producer may override any of them before implementation.

- **Q1 (palette):** "Which palette should colour the card face?" — Answer (agent
  default, recommended): the existing dark `CARD_BG` palette (Food `#5D4037`,
  Culture `#1565C0`, Commerce `#2E7D32`, Service `#6A1B9A`, Entertainment `#C62828`,
  Health `#00838F`), because white card text stays legible; the bright `synergyColor`
  palette stays for icons/accents. Source: repo research of
  `MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.CARD_BG` and `MainStreetCardsUtils.synergyColor`.
  Status: **assumed**.
- **Q2 (split):** "How are a bridge card's two colours arranged?" — Answer (agent
  default, recommended): horizontal split, top band = `synergyTypes[0]`, bottom band =
  `synergyTypes[1]`, matching the operator's wording "two colours top and bottom".
  Source: operator directive. Status: **assumed**.
- **Q3 (scope / render paths):** "Which cards and which generators?" — Answer (agent
  default, recommended): business + community-space cards in all three generators
  (static `.mjs`, runtime CSV TS, dynamic TS); event/upgrade/staff unchanged. Source:
  repo research. Status: **assumed**.

**Research summary (agent, 2026-10-08):** Verified via CSV that bridge cards are the 10
cards with two `synergyTypes` entries and that no card has more than two; located the
two runtime render paths (`MainStreetSvgTextureManager` → static SVGs +
`generateCardSvgFromCsvRow`) and the test-only dynamic `generateBusinessCardSvg`;
confirmed the current face is neutral `#2f2f2f` with synergy only in the accent/header/
icons.

# Restructure the documentation: separate development docs from gameplay docs

**Discovered from:** `MS-0MUNB54KU005084C` (rendering the storyline graph surfaced
that `docs/main-street/` mixes audience-facing gameplay documentation with
engineering/process documentation).

## Problem statement

`docs/main-street/` is a single flat directory that mixes two very different
audiences and lifecycles:

- **Gameplay / player-facing reference** — `storylines.md`,
  `content-design-and-progression.md`, `core-rules-and-mechanics.md`,
  `card-catalog.md`, `card-dimensions.md`, `specialization-skills.md`,
  `ux-visual-audio.md`, `tutorial-localization.md`, `playtest-scenarios.md`,
  `the-build-gdd.md`.
- **Development / engineering & evidence** — `balancing-methodology.md`,
  `balance-analysis-api.md`, `balance-guardrail-recommendations.md`,
  `further-balancing-recommendations.md`, `monte-carlo-*`, `*evidence.md`,
  `prd-*.md`, `ai-strategy.md`, `analysis/`, `screenshots/`, generated
  artefacts (`storyline-graph.mmd`, `storyline-manifest.json`,
  `expanded-card-manifest.json`, `card-catalog-baseline.json`).

A reader looking for gameplay rules has to wade through balance experiments,
PRDs and evidence bundles; an engineer looking for process docs has to filter
out player-facing prose. Links between the two trees are also fragile
(relative paths, `example-games/` staleness — see `MS-0MUNC8AOL0092BE5`).

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the documentation split by audience — gameplay docs
separate from development docs — with stable, cross-linked structure, so each
audience can find what it needs and the docs build/guards stay green.

## Proposed shape (to be confirmed in intake/plan)

- `docs/game/` (or `docs/players/`) — gameplay-rule and content reference.
- `docs/dev/` — engineering, balance methodology, PRDs, evidence, process.
- Generated artefacts under a single `assets/` (or `generated/`) location.
- Cross-links updated; doc-drift guards and path-based tests updated.

## Acceptance Criteria (provisional — to be finalised by intake/plan)

Deferred, low-priority follow-up to `MS-0MUWNTQ5L0075Y38` (Create a card shader). The card shader is being delivered now as a Canvas-compatible effect (Option A). A true GPU shader (Phaser 4 Filters / custom shader programs) requires the WebGL renderer.

## Goal

Move the game from `Phaser.CANVAS` to WebGL (`Phaser.AUTO`/`Phaser.WEBGL`, with Canvas fallback) so that Phaser 4's Filter system and custom shaders become available, and re-enable a true GPU card shader.

## Known scope / risks

- `main.ts` and `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` pin `type: Phaser.CANVAS`.
- `GeometryMask` is **Canvas-only in Phaser 4** (`node_modules/phaser/src/display/mask/GeometryMask.js:27`). It is used by Main Street (`MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` log + street-map masks, `MainStreetScene.logContentMask`) and shared core UI (`core/src/ui/HelpPanel.ts`, `Overlay.ts`, `SettingsPanel.ts`) plus gym scenes — all must migrate to the `Mask` filter / `AddMaskShape`.
- WebGL supports only NORMAL/ADD/MULTIPLY/SCREEN blend modes (of 27); Main Street uses none of the exotic ones.
- WebGL context loss/restoration is a new failure mode; canvas-based SVG textures (`textures.addCanvas` in `core/src/core-engine/SvgHelpers.ts`) and `generateTexture` outputs must survive GPU re-upload.
- CI/test strategy: `createCardGame` documents Canvas as ~10x faster than WebGL under SwiftShader; `TestGamePool` forces Canvas and all browser tests boot Canvas. At least one WebGL browser project (Playwright Chromium + SwiftShader) is needed to exercise WebGL-only features.
- Rendering output is not byte-identical across Canvas/WebGL/GPUs; thumbnail/visual-regression determinism needs re-checking.

## Note

Phaser 4.0.0-rc.7 currently ships only WebGL (no WebGPU). This migration is the necessary intermediate step towards a future WebGL2/WebGPU backend, but it does **not** deliver WebGPU.

## Acceptance Criteria (draft — refine at intake/plan)

1. The game boots under WebGL with a working Canvas fallback and no regression to existing rendering.
2. All `GeometryMask` usages are migrated to the Phaser 4 `Mask` filter (or an equivalent), across Main Street and shared core UI.
3. At least one WebGL browser test project runs in CI and exercises a WebGL-only feature.
4. Full project test suite passes.
5. All related documentation is updated.

# Make card packs available in the browser distribution

**Discovered from:** `MS-0MV0M5BHH0020WFY` (Add a DLC to test the pack unlock and import)

## Problem statement

The card-pack (DLC) channel works under the Electron launcher but is **inert in
the browser distribution** (the GitHub Pages site at
`https://thewizardscode.github.io/tce-main-street/`). In a plain browser the
Card Packs panel opens but always shows "No card packs installed", so the
production residential pack can neither be seen, unlocked, nor played. This
item bundles the production pack into the web distribution and adds a browser
content-unlock client so the whole **lock → purchase → enable → deal** path
works without a launcher content directory.

## Users

- **Browser player** — plays the distributed web build and expects the
  residential DLC to appear, be purchasable and playable.
- **Developer / pack author** — ships a pack and expects the web build to
  bundle it automatically, with no manual `<contentDir>` install step.

Example user stories:

> As a player of the web build, I want the residential card pack to appear in
> the Card Packs panel and be unlockable and playable, so the DLC works in the
> distributed browser version and not only under the Electron launcher.

> As a developer, I want the packs bundled into the web build automatically, so
> shipping a pack needs no manual content-directory install step.

## Existing state

- `bootstrapMainStreetCardPacks()` reads the content directory from
  `window.tce.contentDir` (set only by the Electron preload from
  `TCE_RESOLVED_CONTENT_DIR`). In the browser that is `null`, so
  `shouldBootstrapPacks` (`src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts`)
  returns `false` and `getMainStreetCardPackLoadResult()` stays `null`.
- Pack content lives in `packs/` (source) and is built into the gitignored
  `build/card-packs/packs/`, which a human must copy into
  `<contentDir>/packs/`. Nothing in the web build (`npm run build` → `dist/`)
  includes it.
- Two further Electron-only seams gate the browser path:
  - `resolveCardPackAssetUrl` (`core/src/ui/card-pack-url.ts`) builds pack
    URLs as `tce-packs://<gameId>/<packId>/<path>`; the scheme is served only
    by the Electron `pack-protocol` handler. The core loader
    (`core/src/ui/CardPackLoader.ts`) uses this builder for the pack CSV as
    well as its assets, so the browser cannot read the CSV through it.
  - Content-unlock reads go through `window.tce.contentUnlocks`
    (`core/src/ui/content-unlock-client.ts`); the total client degrades to
    "not unlocked" with no bridge, so even a discovered pack would render
    **locked** with no way to purchase it.
- The launcher content-directory install path (`packs/` → `build/card-packs/`
  → `<contentDir>/packs/`) already works under Electron and must keep working.

## Desired change

Adopt a **pack-source registry** so pack content is resolved from one of
several interchangeable sources rather than hard-wiring the Electron content
directory:

1. **Bundled (build-time) source** — implemented in this item (Option B or C
   below; the implementer records the final shape).
2. **Same-origin static `<base>/packs/`** and **remote URL source** — additive,
   future sources (remote hosting tracked separately by
   `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC`).

Alongside the bundled source, add a **`localStorage`-backed browser
content-unlock client** (reusing the `StorageLike` seam in
`src/MainStreetPrefs.ts`) plus a client-side **rule-scoped simulated-purchase**
rule, so the browser preserves the full lock → purchase → enable flow and the
unlock survives a reload.

### Locked direction (producer, 2026-10-10)

Producer confirmed the source-registry refinement and locked the direction:

- Build the **pack-source registry abstraction** now; the bundled source is
  implemented in this item; remote hosting is the linked follow-up
  `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` (which depends on this item).
- **Bundled source = Option B (virtual registry) or Option C
  (`import.meta.glob`)** — the exact mechanism is an implementation detail for
  the implementer.
- **Browser content unlocks = `localStorage`-backed client** preserving the
  lock → purchase → enable flow.

### Options considered (design record)

- **Option A — static `public/packs/` + same-origin fallback contentDir.**
  Copy `packs/` into `public/packs/`; when `window.tce.contentDir` is absent
  fall back to `import.meta.env.BASE_URL`/`document.baseURI`. Reuses the fetch
  loader unchanged, closest parity with Electron, packs updatable without a JS
  rebuild — but needs a prebuild copy step and a browser equivalent of the
  `tce-packs://` asset URL builder.
- **Option B — build-time virtual pack registry.** A Vite plugin (mirroring
  `gameDiscoveryPlugin` / `virtual:game-registry`) scans `packs/` and emits a
  virtual module; Main Street injects `fetchManifest`/`fetchCsv` transports
  that read from it. Offline, deterministic, follows an established repo
  pattern — but bakes packs into the bundle and needs a plugin + types.
- **Option C — inline `import.meta.glob` bundling (no plugin).** A small
  `bundledPacks.ts` uses `import.meta.glob('../../packs/**/*', …)` for the
  manifest/CSV (`?raw`) and assets (`?url`). No plugin, simplest to implement,
  works in browser and tests — but always bundles every pack (bundle size
  grows) and is Vite-specific.
- **Option D — pre-merge the pack CSV into the base pool at build time.**
  Simple, but loses the DLC gate semantics and does not satisfy the
  "demonstrate the unlock path" intent of `MS-0MV0M5BHH0020WFY`. Rejected.
- **Option E — sibling deployed packs directory.** Mechanically Option A with
  packs as a separate deployment artefact. Still available as a future source.

**Recommendation:** Option C (or B) for the bundled source, unified behind the
pack-source registry, combined with the `localStorage`-backed content-unlock
client. Options A/E remain possible future sources without a rewrite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The web build (`npm run build` → `dist/`) embeds the production residential pack (manifest, `cards.csv` and assets) with **no manual `<contentDir>/packs/` copy step**; a build-artefact assertion proves the pack is present in the emitted `dist/`.
- The pack-source abstraction resolves Main Street card-pack content from at least one non-Electron source (the bundled source) and is structured so a same-origin or remote source can be added **additively** without changing the core loader or the listing (the remote source itself is out of scope — `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC`).
- In the browser build (no `window.tce.contentDir` and no Electron bridges), Main Street boot discovers the bundled pack so the Card Packs panel lists the residential pack instead of "No card packs installed".
- The pack remains **gated** in the browser: while locked its cards stay out of play and its listing row offers a `[ Purchase ]` control.
- A **scoped simulated purchase** (declared rule `main-street-residential-pack-purchase`) flips the pack to unlocked and to `[ Enable ]`; enabling it merges its rows so its cards deal in play. A test covers the lock → purchase → enable → deal path in the browser source.
- The simulated purchase is **rule-scoped**: it does not collateral-unlock any other configured reward (for example the itch.io golf reward).
- Browser content-unlock state **persists across a page reload** through the `localStorage`-backed client, and the existing enabled-pack preference continues to persist.
- Pack CSV and asset URLs **resolve in the browser with no `tce-packs://` request**; either the bundled source supplies same-origin/relative URLs or the pack assets are demonstrably unused for card rendering.
- **Electron behaviour is unchanged**: with `window.tce.contentDir` set, discovery still reads the content directory through the existing `tce-packs://` protocol, and the content-directory install path remains supported.
- Save/load and missing/disabled-pack degradation continue to behave as they do under Electron, covered by focused browser-path regression tests.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (specifically `README.md`, `packs/README.md`, `DEPLOYMENT.md`, `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md`).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Do **not** change the Electron content-directory install path; it must remain
  supported (behavioural parity).
- The browser must remain functional with **no Electron bridges** — every new
  client degrades totally (never throws), matching the existing
  `createContentUnlockClient` / `loadCardPacks` total-degradation contract.
- Reuse existing seams (`StorageLike` in `src/MainStreetPrefs.ts`;
  `fetchManifest`/`fetchCsv`/`loader` overrides in `MainStreetCardPacks.ts`;
  the `virtual:game-registry` plugin pattern) rather than inventing parallel
  mechanisms.
- Pack content is bundled at build time — changing a bundled pack requires a
  rebuild in this iteration (runtime-updatable packs are the remote-source
  follow-up).
- Packs must stay licence-clean and project-generated (existing constraint from
  `packs/README.md`).
- The web base path is derived from the package name (GitHub Pages project
  site); any same-origin fallback must respect `import.meta.env.BASE_URL`.

## Out of scope

- Real storefront/Steam purchase wiring.
- A pack-authoring/store UI.
- Changing the Electron content-directory install path.
- Remote hosting of pack bundles (`MS-0MV26X8T200852AC`).
- Additional packs beyond the residential set.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts` — pack-source registry wiring; browser fallback
  content source; injected transports.
- `src/MainStreetContentUnlockGate.ts` — wire the browser content-unlock client
  into entitlement resolution.
- `src/MainStreetPrefs.ts` — `localStorage`-backed unlock store (reusing
  `StorageLike`).
- `core/src/ui/content-unlock-client.ts` — a bundled/localStorage-backed client
  compatible with the existing total client interface.
- `vite.config.ts` — pack bundling plugin (Option B) or a prebuild copy step.
- `core/scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.*` — pattern reference for a
  `virtual:card-pack-registry` plugin (if Option B).
- `packs/` / `public/packs/` — bundled pack source/artefact.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` — boot gate that must
  trigger discovery in the browser.
- `core/src/ui/CardPackLoader.ts` / `core/src/ui/card-pack-url.ts` — URL
  resolution seam (avoid `tce-packs://` in the browser path).
- `tests/main-street/` — browser pack discovery, unlock/purchase persistence,
  and build-artefact tests.
- `README.md`, `packs/README.md`, `DEPLOYMENT.md`, `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` —
  docs.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep.** The registry abstraction invites building the remote source
  now. Mitigation: remote hosting stays a linked follow-up
  (`MS-0MV26X8T200852AC`); the abstraction only needs to admit it additively.
- **Supply-chain (future).** A remote pack injects card rows; the merge
  contract rejects bad headers/duplicate ids but not malicious content. The
  remote follow-up must add signing/hashing plus the unlock gate — recorded
  there, not built here.
- **Bundle size.** Option C always bundles every pack. Assumption: the single
  residential pack (10 cards + PNGs) is small enough; if it grows, Option B
  (opt-in registry) is available.
- **Duplicate unlock state.** A browser `localStorage` unlock client plus the
  Electron unified store could disagree. Assumption: the local client is used
  only when no Electron bridge is present; precedence is explicit and tested.
- **Gate semantics drift.** Bundling must not accidentally pre-unlock the pack
  (Option D's failure mode); the lock → purchase → enable assertions guard it.
- **Base-path correctness.** Same-origin URLs must work under the GitHub Pages
  project base (`/<package>/`), not just `/`.

## Related work

- **Parent context:** `MS-0MV0M5BHH0020WFY` — Add a DLC to test the pack unlock
  and import (this item's discovery source).
- **Depends on / dependencies:**
  `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` — Remote hosting of card packs (remote bundle source)
  **depends on this item** (blocked).
- **Related implementations:** `MS-0MV0OK0XU0062E0H` (pack listing UI & boot
  wiring, completed), `MS-0MV07GNUU005E536` (pack merge & persistence,
  completed), `MS-0MV0Q479I002W0R6` (end-to-end pipeline test, completed),
  `MS-0MV16VYN3006SWM4` (content-unlock entitlement gate, open),
  `MS-0MV16VYYB000TI7H` (scoped simulated purchase, open),
  `MS-0MV26K321003MWO0` (pack assets self-contained, in progress).
- **Docs:** `packs/README.md`, `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `DEPLOYMENT.md`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUR9IMXE0090WIV** – Confirm win thresholds / run length as the difficulty lever after the rebalance (open)
- **MS-0MV1HAI5G005Q3RT** – [test-failure] composite-click.browser.test.ts > composite click deducts the premium for business and community-space cards via the dialog — failing test (completed)
- **MS-0MUQZH6Z50035KVU** – Deployment documentation (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: absent, acceptance, add, additional, also (+320 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: absent, acceptance, add, additional, also (+282 more)
- `core/README.md` — matched: add, also, always, appear, artefact (+193 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Which pack-bundling mechanism should be used (Option A–E), and does it
  need to support remotely hosted bundles? — **Answer (producer, `MS-C0MV26XJNF00751OW` / `MS-C0MV26LA70005X6NS`):** Adopt a **pack-source registry**;
  build the abstraction now, implement the **bundled** source in this item
  (Option B or C), and leave remote hosting to the linked follow-up
  `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC`. Option B alone cannot host remote bundles; remote is a
  runtime source the registry admits additively. Source: worklog comments.
- **Q:** How is the browser lock → purchase → enable flow preserved? —
  **Answer (producer, `MS-C0MV26XJNF00751OW`):** Add a **`localStorage`-backed
  content-unlock client** plus a client-side scoped simulated-purchase rule.
  Source: worklog comment.
- **Q:** Does this item change the Electron content-directory install path? —
  **Answer:** No; it remains supported and out of scope. Source: existing work
  item description ("Out of scope").
- **Q:** Should real storefront/Steam purchase be wired? — **Answer:** No;
  simulated purchase only, as elsewhere in the DLC pipeline. Source: existing
  work item description.

No open questions remain; the direction was locked by the producer on
2026-10-10.

# Console noise when running the tutorial (tf factory + zone collision warnings)

## Problem statement

Starting (and playing) the Main Street tutorial floods the browser console with developer warnings that are not actionable: `[tfAdapter] Missing tf factory for key "income-positive-chime" ...` and repeated `Zone collision for "<hand|endTurnButton|incidentQueue>" while composing "main-street-canonical" with "main-street-tutorial" ...`. The noise obscures genuine errors and breaks "clean console" expectations for the tutorial boot path, while gameplay itself is unaffected.

Seed context: browser client console log captured while running the tutorial (`client:789`, 2026-10-10).

## Users

- **Developer / QA engineer** running the tutorial locally who needs a clean console so real errors are visible.
- **Automated browser tests / release checks** that treat unexpected console errors/warnings as failures.

Example user stories:

- As a developer, I want booting and playing the tutorial to emit no unexpected console warnings, so that any real error stands out immediately.
- As a QA engineer, I want the remaining intentional diagnostics to be explicit and quiet by default, so that I do not re-triage known-benign warnings.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Booting/playing the tutorial at the canonical 1280×720 viewport emits **no** `[tfAdapter] Missing tf factory ...` warning for the four intentionally factory-less SFX mappings (`sfx-income-positive`, `sfx-income-negative`, `sfx-income-neutral`, `sfx-challenge-complete`), while each of those keys still falls back to the WAV path (verified by test).
2. Booting the tutorial emits **no** `Zone collision ...` warning for `hand`, `endTurnButton`, or `incidentQueue` when composing `main-street-canonical` with `main-street-tutorial`, while the `sceneWins` result still resolves the tutorial zone rects (verified by test).
3. Unexpected diagnostics remain detectable: a genuinely missing factory or an unapproved zone collision can still be surfaced/asserted by tests rather than being silently swallowed (verified by test).
4. At least one regression test asserts the tutorial boot path produces no warnings from either source; `tests/main-street/tfFallback.test.ts`, `core/tests/ui/screen-layout-compose.test.ts`, and `tests/main-street/tutorial-layout-resolution.test.ts` all still pass.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Preserve the existing WAV/Phaser fallback for factory-less SFX keys (engine contract CG-0MUU9PSWC009CW76) — no silent drops.
- Do **not** add new ToneForge recipes/factories in this item (larger separate effort; see risks).
- Preserve `sceneWins` composition semantics and the tutorial alignment contract documented in `MainStreetTutorialHints.ts`; tutorial zone rects must not change.
- The fix must not blind future diagnostics — intentional cases are suppressed/deduplicated, not the detection removed.

## Existing state

- `core/src/core-engine/tfAdapter.ts` (`createTfPlayer`) defaults to a `console.warn` logger. `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` calls `createTfPlayer(tfModule)` / `createTfPlayer(loadedModule)` without a logger, so every factory-less key warns on play.
- The committed runtime synth (`core/src/core-engine/tf-runtime/main-street-runtime-synth.mjs`) ships 12 factories, while `src/sfx-tf-mapping.ts` maps 16 logical keys; the 4 extra keys intentionally fall back to WAV (codified in `tests/main-street/tfFallback.test.ts`).
- `core/src/ui/screen-layout-compose.ts` emits `ZONE_COLLISION` as `console.warn` when no `reportIssue` hook is supplied. `src/scenes/MainStreetTutorialHints.ts` (`resolveMarketCardAnchor` and `resolveZoneToAnchor`) calls `composeResolvedLayouts(BASE_LAYOUT, TUTORIAL_LAYOUT, …, { policy: 'sceneWins' })` with no hook, so the documented intentional overrides (`hand`, `endTurnButton`, `incidentQueue`, `developmentRow`) warn on every resolution.

## Desired change

- Make the intentional audio fallback silent (or debug-level, one-shot) in production wiring, while keeping the fallback behaviour and the ability to surface unexpected missing factories.
- Make the tutorial's known-intentional zone collisions quiet (e.g. via a `reportIssue` hook that ignores/deduplicates the documented override zones), while keeping unexpected collisions visible.
- Add regression tests pinning both.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` — pass a quiet/debug logger to `createTfPlayer` at both call sites (~lines 253, ~278).
- `core/src/core-engine/SoundManager.ts` — keep the fallback path quiet/debug for known factory-less keys (~lines 300–330, 505–515).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTutorialHints.ts` — pass a `reportIssue` hook to both `composeResolvedLayouts` calls (~lines 159, ~203).
- `core/src/ui/screen-layout-compose.ts` — only if the composer needs a quiet/dedupe option; keep the public contract intact.
- `src/sfx-tf-mapping.ts` — annotate the four intentionally factory-less mappings.
- Tests: `tests/main-street/tfFallback.test.ts`, `core/tests/ui/screen-layout-compose.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/tutorial-layout-resolution.test.ts`, plus a tutorial boot console-cleanliness test.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the four factory-less mappings are intended to use WAV fallback (evidence: `tests/main-street/tfFallback.test.ts` header + engine child CG-0MUU9PSWC009CW76). We silence the warning rather than add synth factories.
- **Assumption:** tutorial zone-name reuse is intentional (evidence: alignment-contract comment in `MainStreetTutorialHints.ts`). We silence the intentional collision rather than rename zones.
- **Risk:** over-suppressing warnings hides a real missing factory / accidental collision. Mitigation: suppress only known keys/zones; add a test-visible reporter and keep unexpected issues visible.
- **Risk (scope creep):** adding the four missing synth factories (income positive/negative/neutral, challenge-complete) is a distinct, larger effort — record as a linked follow-up instead of expanding this item.
- **Risk:** console assertions are environment-sensitive; the regression test must target the specific warning messages, not "no console output at all".

## Related work

### Manual

- **MS-0MUU9QYQE006NLEZ** – Activate ToneForge runtime synth: loader diagnostics + scene wiring (completed) — established the fallback contract and diagnostics this item makes quiet. Engine sibling child: **CG-0MUU9PSWC009CW76**.
- **MS-0MUQ1KXAS003FJ42** – Ship web-based copy of Main Street (GitHub Pages) — release/web context.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUQ1KXAS003FJ42** – Ship web-based copy of Main Street (GitHub Pages) (completed)
- **MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E** – Assign dedicated card art to every Main Street card (1024×1024 source; eliminate generic Fallback art) (open)
- **MS-0MUYK08I1004I19W** – Upgrade-deck composition lever: raise level-2 capstone reachability (market weight / copies) (completed)
